1STR: Saaee = that very. Jaai = place. Samhaal = (under the letter 'm' of this word there is a half 'h'). Jithai hee = where at last. Vannjana = to go. Maal = wealth. ||58||
Remember too that place where you must go at last. ||58||
Remember that place where you must go. ||58||
Remember you that place, where you have to go.
Keep in mind that place of the next world into which you must go; meaning, do some good deeds for happiness in the next world. ||58||
NUWN: Jinhee = (here there is a half 'h' with the letter 'n'). Jinhee kammee = in which deeds. Gun = gain. Kammrre = ugly deeds.
O Farid! Give up those ugly deeds in which there is no gain (for the soul),
Fareed, those deeds which do not bring merit - forget about those deeds.
Farid! Abandon all those deeds, which are of no avail,
Sri Farid ji says: forget those deeds — those misdeeds — from which there is no gain of the quality of happiness.
KWSW: Theevahee = you may become. Dai = (why 'de' has become 'dai'.) Darbaar = in the court. Dai darbaar = in the court of. ||59||
lest you have to be ashamed in the court of the Master (Parmatma). ||59||
Otherwise, you shall be put to shame, in the Court of the Lord. ||59||
lest you be put to shame in the court of the Lord.
For lest, by doing misdeeds, you be ashamed in the Master's court; so worship. ||59||
2K6L: Bharaand = (for the sake of the 'poison shoots') delusion, confusion, doubt, wandering. Laah = taking off, putting away. Chaakree = service, (that is,) worship.
O Farid! Putting away the wandering of (your) heart (for the sake of these 'poison shoots'), worship the Master (Prabhu).
Fareed, work for your Lord and Master; dispel the doubts of your heart.
Farid! Perform you the service of your Lord and dispel the doubt of your mind.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Serve the Master, and take off — that is, put away — the wandering of the mind.
J9E6: Lorreeai = is needed. Jeeraand = patience, forbearance. Darves = fakir. No = to. ||60||
Fakirs ought to have (the) forbearance of trees. ||60||
The dervishes, the humble devotees, have the patient endurance of trees. ||60||
The saints ought to have the endurance like the trees.
For Parmeshvar's darveshes ought to hold a forbearance like that of (rukhaan) trees. As when someone throws a brick or the like at trees, they give him flowers, fruit, wood and so on. ||60||
75HD: O Farid! (Within me there is not the forbearance of trees that should be in a fakir; like fakirs,) my clothes (indeed) are black, my garb is black,
Fareed, my clothes are black, and my outfit is black.
Farid! Black are my clothes and black is my vestment.
Sri Farid ji says: my clothes too are black — that is, blue — and the (ves) — that is, the colour of my body too — is turning black.
YX8D: Gunahee = with sins. Phiraa = I go about. Lok = the world. Kahai = says. ||61||
(but because of 'bharaand' for the sake of the 'poison shoots') I go about full of sins, and the world calls me a fakir. ||61||
I wander around full of sins, and yet people call me a dervish - a holy man. ||61||
I wander about soiled by sins and people call me a saint.
I go about full of sins, and (lok) people call me a (darves) fakir; meaning, there is no quality of a fakir in me. ||61||
5MH9: Tatee = hot, burnt. Toi = in water. Palvai = thrives, flourishes. Jal = in water.
A crop burnt in water does not turn green (again), even if (someone) drowns (that crop) in water.
The crop which is burnt will not bloom, even if it is soaked in water.
The crop that is destroyed by water, can never bloom even if it be kept dipped in water.

Just as a crop that has (tatee) burned from being watered with (toi) water — even if it is then dipped and drowned in water, still that crop does not (palvai) spread again. So too those who, by reading the Vedas and Shastras, have become clever scholars do not become endowed with good qualities even by the water of teaching, with its many illustrations and proofs.
35M3: Dohaagan = deserted, ill-fated, unfortunate, abandoned. Jhoorede jhoorei = always grieves. Je = even if. ||62||

O Farid! (In the same way the soul-bride who, even while walking on God's path on her own terms,) is separated from God always suffers (that is, even in a fakir's dress, if the mind stays full of sins; even as a darvesh, if 'bharaand' stays in the mind for the sake of the 'poison shoots'; even while staying in the sangat, if the mind stays in doubts — then nothing but grief is in one's lot). ||62||
Fareed, she who is forsaken by her Husband Lord, grieves and laments. ||62||
Farid! She, who is forsaken by God, continues to repent and grieve.
Sri Farid ji says: the soul-bride of (rab) Parmeshvar who has become (dohaagan) deserted keeps grieving again and again. ||62||
KSBH: Veevaahee = married, when she was married. Maamle = quarrels, entanglements.
When (a girl) is unmarried, then she has eagerness (for marriage); (but when) she is married, entanglements come.
When she is a virgin, she is full of desire; but when she is married, then her troubles begin.
When the girl is a virgin, then she is full of desire and when she is married, then begin her troubles.
When this soul-bride was unmarried — that is, alive — she lived in many kinds of eagerness; and when she was married to Yama — that is, when the breaths parted — (maamle) troubles fell upon her.
B0MK: Pachhotaau = regret. Vat = again. Na theeai = cannot become. Jaan = when. Taan = then. ||63||
O Farid! (At that time) there is just this regret: she cannot become unmarried again (that is, that first eagerness cannot arise in her mind again). ||63||
Fareed, she has this one regret, that she cannot be a virgin again. ||63||
Farid! She has this regret, that she cannot be a virgin again.

Sri Farid ji says: then she has just this regret: "Would that I were unmarried again." But she cannot become unmarried again; meaning, she wants a human birth again, but it is not gained. Or: in the maidenhood of seeking there was an eagerness to meet the Guru; and when she was married — that is, met gurus given to worldly activity — they put the troubles of worldly activity upon her; then there is just this regret, that she might return to the maidenhood of detachment; but that does not happen. When there was the maidenhood of seeking, this soul-bride had an eagerness to meet Parmeshvar the Husband; and when she was married — became one with Brahm through the Guru's teaching — then, knowing (maa) Maya and the other vices to be false, she (male) removed them. Then neither regret nor maidenhood occurs; meaning, she becomes free of birth and death. ||63||
TB1J: Keree = of. Aai ulathe = alighted. Hanjh = swans.
Swans alight in a pond of salty earth;
The swans have landed in a small pond of salt water.
The swans have alighted in a small pond of saline water.
In the pond of the salty land of the world, salty with many pains, the (hanjh) swans — the saints — have come and alighted.
3E61: Chinjoo = beak. Borranhi = dip. Sandee = of. Danjh = longing. ||64||
(those swans) dip (their) beaks (in the pond), (but) do not drink (that dirty water); they keep longing to fly away from there. ||64||
They dip in their bills, but do not drink; they fly away, still thirsty. ||64||
They dip in their bills, but drink not, and fly away thirsty.

They dip their beaks in it — that is, through the senses they take things only for practical use — but they do not drink; that is, they do not take them with a mind for enjoyment. They keep a (danjh) longing to fly from the pond of the world — that is, to die. The meaning is: knowing death to be true, they do not turn towards sense-objects. ||64||
BU3W: Udd = flying. Kodhrai = in a field of kodhra millet. Paia = alighted, sat. Viddaaran = to drive away.
A swan flew and settled in a field of kodhra millet; then the people of the world go to drive it away.
The swans fly away, and land in the fields of grain. The people go to chase them away.
Flying away, the swans alight on the barley-farm and men go to drive them away.
Just as a swan, flying, went where kodhra, a coarse grain, grows, and people go to drive it off, so that it does not eat their kodhra —
LVYK: Gahla = crazy. Lok = the world, (that is,) the people of the world. ||65||
The crazy world does not know that the swan does not eat kodhra. ||65||
The thoughtless people do not know, that the swans do not eat the grain. ||65||
The headless mortals know not, that the swans eat not the coarse grain.

but that crowd of people, who are (gahila) crazy, do not know this: the swan does not eat kodhra at all. Illustration: in the same way, if a saint happens to go into some householder's house, and they suspect him of sense-pleasures — those crazy, self-willed people do not know that these saints never accept sense-pleasures. ||65||
CKD6: Chal chal gaeeaan = went away, each in turn. Pankheeaan = flocks of birds. Tal = pool. Vasaae = were bringing life to.
O Farid! The flocks of (soul-)birds that have made this (world-)pool beautiful are going away (leaving it), each in their turn.
The birds which lived in the pools have flown away and left.
The birds, which peopled the pools, have flown away.
The kings such as Prithu who (vasaae) settled villages on the earth — that is, laid down order — those ranks of kings, like flocks of birds, have gone restlessly from this world.
N9M7: Sar = pool, lake. Chalsee = will dry up. Thake = withered. Ikal = left behind alone. ||66||
(This world-)pool too will dry up, and the lotuses left behind alone will wither too (that is, all the beautiful things of creation will perish). ||66||
Fareed, the overflowing pool shall also pass away, and only the lotus flowers shall remain. ||66||
Farid! The brimful lake shall also pass away and lotus flowers alone shall remain.

Sri Farid ji says: this pool of the world, filled with the water of name and form, will also (chalsee) go entirely — that is, be destroyed. So the saints in it who, unattached like the lotus, have become (ikal) dwellers in solitude, have (thake) stayed steady through their oneness with Brahm; for no one has stayed steady in the world in the body. ||66||
KU0H: It siraane = a brick will be under the head. Bhui = in the earth. Maas = in the flesh, in the body.

O Farid! (Like the flocks of soul-birds going away, when your turn comes, you too) will have a brick under your head, you will lie asleep in the earth (that is, in the grave), (and) worms will crawl in your body.
Fareed, a stone will be your pillow, and the earth will be your bed. The worms shall eat into your flesh.
Farid! Brick shall be your pillow, the earth your bed to sleep and the worms shall eat your flesh.

Sri Farid ji says: having died, one sleeps in the earth in the grave with a brick placed under the head, and then a swarm of worms bites into the flesh. Or: when the worm of death bit into the body, then came such a sleep in the grave.
111W: Ketarria jug = many ages, endless time. Vaapre = will pass. Ikat paas = on one side. ||67||
(In this way) a very long time will pass lying on one side (then no one will wake you; so do not sleep heedless now). ||67||
Countless ages will pass, and you will still be lying on one side. ||67||
Good many ages shall pass away and you shall continue to lye on one side.
Then many ages pass for those lying on one side, and worms keep biting and eating the flesh of those (vaapre) poor ones. ||67|| ☬ These two saloks too were uttered at Faridkot. So now he says:
K10P: Savannvee = of beautiful colour. Gharree = the vessel of the body. Naagar = beautiful. Laj = rope (the chain of breaths).
O Farid! (See — some person's body, a) vessel of beautiful colour, has broken (next door to you), (and the) beautiful rope (of breaths) has snapped.
Fareed, your beautiful body shall break apart, and the subtle thread of the breath shall be snapped.
Farid the beauteous body pitcher, shall break and the sublime rope of breath shall be snapped.
Sri Farid ji says: this pitcher of the body, which was of (savannvee) excellent colour, will break — that is, die; the (naagar) excellent (laj) rope of the breaths will snap.
A1KQ: Kai ghar = in whose house? Naathee = guest. ||68||

(See,) in whose house is the angel (of death), Azrael, a guest today? (that is, if every day before you, from the flocks of soul-birds, someone or other's turn to leave comes, then why are you sleeping heedless?) ||68||
In which house will the Messenger of Death be a guest today? ||68||
In whose house shall Azaril, the death's courier, be the guest today?
Azrael the angel, the messenger of Dharam Raja, will today be a (naathee) guest in someone's house; meaning, he will be the guest of King Mokalhar. ||68||
0PJL: O Farid! (See, whose body,) the vessel of beautiful colour, has broken, (and the) beautiful rope (of breaths) has snapped?
Fareed, your beautiful body shall break apart, and the subtle thread of the breath shall be snapped.
Farid! The beauteous body pitcher shall break and the sublime rope of breath shall sunder.
Sri Farid ji says: the pitcher of the body, of beautiful colour, has broken, and the beautiful rope of the breaths has snapped.
5Q61: Bhui = on the earth. Bhaar the = were (only) a burden (that is, they had forgotten the purpose of birth). Kiu aavahi aj = how can they come again today? (that is,) this time of human birth is not found again. ||69||
Those brothers who (heedless of namaz) remained (only) a burden on the earth will not find this time of human birth again. ||69||
Those friends who were a burden on the earth - how can they come today? ||69||
The friends, who were a burden on the earth, how can they return today?
The friends, the kings, who were the support of the earth — how can they come into this body today? The meaning is: now they cannot come. ||69||
1LXV: O Farid! Those people who do not offer namaz (that is, who are heedless of worship) are (like) dogs; this way of living of theirs cannot be called good,
Fareed: O faithless dog, this is not a good way of life.
Farid! You are like a dog who does no prayer; this is not a good habit on yours.
Sri Farid ji says: O dog of a man without namaz! It is not a good way for you to be without worship.
QK3A: Kab hee = ever. Chal na aaia = did not come walking, did not make the effort to come. Benivaaja = those who do not offer namaz, who do not worship. ||70||
(because they) never make the effort to come to the mosque at the five times (that is, they never remember God even five times a day at the least). ||70||
You never come to the mosque for your five daily prayers. ||70||
You come not ever to the mosque five times a day for prayer.
For at the five times of namaz you have never walked to the mosque. ||70||
T9M7: Uju = washing hands, face and feet before offering namaz. Uju saaj = do the ablution, wash face and hands. Subah = of the morning. Nivaaj gujaar = offer namaz.
O Farid! Get up, wash your face and hands, and offer the morning namaz.
Rise up, Fareed, and cleanse yourself; chant your morning prayer.
Farid! Wake up and perform your ablution and say your morning prayer.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Get up, do the ablution, and spend this time offering the morning namaz.
72AK: The head that does not bow before the Master, God — cut that head off and remove it (that is, what is the use of living for a person without worship?) ||71||
The head which does not bow to the Lord - chop off and remove that head. ||71||
The head, which bows not to the Lord, chop off the remove you that head.
For the head that does not bow to (saanee) Parmeshvar — cut that head off and take it from the trunk. ||71||
2QNU: Keejai kaai = what should we do with it? What should we make of it?
The head that does not bow before the Master, God (in worship) — that head is of no use.
That head which does not bow to the Lord - what is to be done with that head?
The head, which bows not to the Lord, what is to be done with such a head?
The head that does not bow to the Master — that is, does not touch the forehead to the ground — what is that head to be done with? Meaning, it will be of no use.
EUWV: That head should be burned under the cooking pot in place of firewood (that is, take that stiff, unbending head to be just dry wood). ||72||
Put it in the fireplace, instead of firewood. ||72||
Burn it you under the earthen pot, in place of fire-wood.
Let that head be burned in place of firewood under the (kunna) pot — the dyer's dye-vat that stays on the fire day and night. ||72||
Y0EE: Taidde = your. Too = you. Jaanioh = gave birth. Jinhee = under the letter 'n' of this word there is a half 'h'.
O Farid! (If you do not think of the other flocks of soul-birds going away, then just see:) where are your (own) parents, who gave birth to you? Those parents of yours left you long ago.
Fareed, where are your mother and father, who gave birth to you?
Farid! Today, where are your parents who gave you birth?
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! The mother and father who brought you into being — where are they now? Meaning, they have died.
TWL4: Pateenohi = were convinced, were satisfied, came to believe. Oi = those parents of yours (plural of the word 'oh'). ||73||
You still have not come to believe (that you too must go from here; that is why you lie heedless of worshipping God). ||73||
They have left you, but even so, you are not convinced that you shall also have to go. ||73||
They have departed from you, even then, you are not convinced that you too shall die.
They have gone from you, out of this world; but you are still not (pateenohi) convinced; meaning, you have not yet come to believe in your own death. ||73||
PHY7: Maidaan = level ground. Laah = remove. Toe tibe = low and high places.
O Farid! Make the mind level, (and) remove (its) high and low places,
Fareed, flatten out your mind; smooth out the hills and valleys.
Farid! Make your mind even by smoothing hollows and heaps.

Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Removing the pits and mounds of ignorance and ego — or the thoughts and counter-thoughts — make the mind clean like level ground; meaning, purify it by becoming free of vices.
ALNL: Agai = ahead of you, on the journey of your life. Sandee = of. Bhaah = fire. Aavasee = will come. ||74||

(if you can do this, then) the fire of hell will not come at all on your life's journey (that is, the troubles that befall a person because pits and mounds stay in the mind will vanish once these are removed). ||74||
Hereafter, the fires of hell shall not even approach you. ||74||
The fire of hell shall not ever approach you thereafter.
For by following this way, the fire of hell will not come to you ahead at all; meaning, you will become free of the pain of the hells. ||74||
78TA: Khaalak = Parmatma, who brings creation into being. Maahi = in.
O Farid! Parmatma (the Creator of creation) is present in (all) creation, and creation lives in Parmatma.
Fareed, the Creator is in the Creation, and the Creation abides in God.
Farid! The Creator abides in creation and the creation abides in Creator.

Sri Guru ji says through Farid: that Vahiguru is dwelling in all (khalak) creation, and all creation is dwelling in that Creator; meaning, He Himself has become the form of all. As it is said: 'Through and through He pervades every form and colour.'
RAGP: When there is no other at all apart from that Parmatma, then which being can be called bad? (that is, no person can be called bad). ||75||
Whom can we call bad? There is none without Him. ||75||
When there is none without Him, whom should we call as bad?
When there is no one other than Him, then whom should we call bad? ||75|| ☬ He points to detachment:
1YBV: Ji dih = on which day. Naala = umbilical cord. Kapahi = (you) had cut (O midwife!). Chukh = a little.
O Farid! (O midwife!) On the day you cut my cord, if you had cut my throat a little too,
Fareed, if on that day when my umbilical cord was cut, my throat had been cut instead,
Farid! If my throat too had been cut a bit on the day my navel string was cut,
Sri Farid ji says: on the day the midwife cut the cord, if at that time she had cut the throat a (chukh) little as well,
UNA1: Itee = so many. Maamle = entanglements, troubles. ||76||
then I would not have fallen into so many entanglements (because of these pits and mounds of the mind), nor would I have borne so many pains. ||76||
I would not have fallen into so many troubles, or undergone so many hardships. ||76||
I should not have fallen into so many troubles nor undergone so many hardships.
then so many painful (maamle) troubles would not have come, and I would not have borne so many pains. ||76||
0K6W: Chaban = teeth, chewers. Chalan = legs. Ratann = eyes. Suneear = ears. Se = those (on whose pride the pits and mounds were built in the mind, on whose pride I used to think others lowly). Bah gae = sat down, became idle, stopped working.

(On what pride were others called bad? On what pride were these pits and mounds made in the mind?) Those teeth, legs, eyes and ears (on whose pride these pits and mounds were made) have stopped working.
My teeth, feet, eyes and ears have stopped working.
My teeth, feet, eyes, and ears; they have ceases their functions.
The teeth that chewed, the feet that walked, the eyes that were like jewels, and the (suneear) ears and all the other senses have (bah gae) gone from their own work — that is, become unable.
9T4A: Herre = the body. Dhaah mutee = cried aloud. Se jaanee = those friends (on whom there was pride). ||77||
(This) body has cried out (that is, this very body of one's own is now grieving that) those friends of mine have gone (that is, have stopped serving — the ones I was proud of). ||77||
My body cries out, "Those whom I knew have left me!" ||77||
my body cried out a loud lamentation, " those intimates of mine have abandoned me".
When those (jaanee) friends who had been with it from the beginning had all gone, then the (herre) body let out a cry of weeping; meaning, in old age all the limbs grow slack. ||77||
7F3V: Man = in the mind. Na hadhaai = do not let in.
O Farid! Do good even to the one who does bad. Do not let anger come into your mind.
Fareed, answer evil with goodness; do not fill your mind with anger.
Farid! Do good deeds for evil and harbour not wrath in your mind.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Do good even to the bad; do not (hadhaai) keep anger in the mind.

EMQP: Dehee = to the body. Na lagaee = does not strike. Sabh kichh = everything. Palai paai = stays in one's lap, stays safe. ||78||
(In this way) no disease strikes the body, and every treasure (that is, every good quality) stays safe. ||78||
Your body shall not suffer from any disease, and you shall obtain everything. ||78||
Your body shall be infested with no disease and you shall obtain everything.
The disease of ego will not strike the subtle body, and you will gather all the fruits — dharma, wealth, desire, liberation and the rest — into the lap of the heart. ||78||
A82B: Pankh = flock of birds. Dunee = the world. Suhaava = beautiful.
O Farid! This world is a beautiful garden (why make 'pits and mounds' in the mind here? Here the whole) flock of (soul-)birds is only a guest.
Fareed, the bird is a guest in this beautiful world-garden.
Farid! The soul-bird is a guest in the beauteous world garden.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! In this garden of the world, which is looking beautiful, the flock of soul-birds is like a guest; meaning, it stays only a short while.
8DPD: Naubat = kettledrum. Subah siu = of the morning. Saaj = provisions, preparation, readiness. ||79||
When the morning drum sounds (all must cut short the night of life and go). (O Farid! Remove these 'pits and mounds', and you too) make ready to go. ||79||
The morning drums are beating - get ready to leave! ||79||
The drum of the morn beats. Make you preparation for your departure.
So for this being, from (subah) birth onwards, the drum — the Vedas, or death — keeps sounding. It says just this: "O being! Make ready the provisions for leaving; meaning, do good deeds." ||79||
LLVY: O Farid! (That preparation can be made only at night:) musk is shared out in (the solitude of) the night (that is, in the solitude of night the fragrance of worship arises); those who stay asleep get no share (of it).
Fareed, musk is released at night. Those who are sleeping do not receive their share.
Farid! The musk is spread (in air) at night, and they, who remain asleep get not a share.

Sri Farid ji says: in the night of one's lifespan the (kathooree) musk of devotion is shared out; but those asleep in the sleep of ignorance do not get the (bhaau) portion — that is, the share — of that devotion.
5JRL: Jinha, tinha = here under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'. Needraavle = heavy with sleep. Milan = meeting, attainment. Kuaau = from where? how? ||80||
Those whose eyes stay heavy with sleep (all night) — how can they attain (the musk of the Name)? ||80||
Those whose eyes are heavy with sleep - how can they receive it? ||80||
They, whose eyes are heavy with sleep, how can they be blessed with it?
Those whose eyes are heavy with sleep — (kuaau) how can their meeting with Parmeshvar happen? Meaning, those who worship, free of sleep, become one with Parmeshvar. ||80||
X245: Mujh koo = to me. Sabaaiai jag = in the whole world.

O Farid! I (at first, troubled by the pain born of the 'pits and mounds' of the mind,) thought that the pain was (only) mine (that only I was in pain); (but in truth this) pain is (spread) through the whole world.
Fareed, I thought that I was in trouble; the whole world is in trouble!
Farid! I thought, I alone was in trouble, however, in fact the whole world is in trouble.
Sri Farid ji says: I had thought that the pain was mine alone, but the beings of the whole world are in pain.
8KXR: Ooche charr kai = rising above pain. Ghar = in the house. Ghar ghar = in every house. Ag = (the spelling of this word is worth noting: it always ends in (i); the original word is Sanskrit 'agni', and from this the Prakrit form is 'agi'). ||81||
When I rose above (my own pain) (and looked), I saw that this same fire is (burning) in every house (that is, every being is in pain). ||81||
When I climbed the hill and looked around, I saw this fire in each and every home. ||81||
When I looked around from an elevation, then did I find the same fire in every house.
When, withdrawing from the body and becoming steady in detachment, I looked, then in every house — that is, in the bodies of all beings — this fire of pain appeared. ||81||
U3Y0: Bhoom = earth. Rangaavalee = rang-aavalee. Aavalee = row, sequence. Rang = beauty, joy, bliss. Rangaavalee = delightful. Manjh = in (it). Visoola = full of poison, poisonous. Nivaajia = honoured, exalted.
O Farid! (This) earth is delightful, (but because of the pits and mounds of the human mind) a poisonous garden (has grown) in (it) (in which the fire of pains is burning).
Fareed, in the midst of this beautiful earth, there is a garden of thorns.
Farid! In the midst of the beauteous world there is a thorny garden.

Sri Guru ji says through Sri Farid ji: O brother! This earth of the intellect was (rangaavalee) full of bliss. In its (manjh) midst a garden of thorns in particular has grown green; meaning, trees of thorns such as lust and anger have sprung up.
MWQK: Tinha = (under the letter 'n' of this word there is a half 'h'). Anch = heat, scorch. Peer = murshid, Guru. ||82||
In which [sic: likely 'the people whom'] the True Guru has raised high — the heat (of the fire of pain) does not touch them. ||82||
Those humble beings who are blessed by their spiritual teacher, do not suffer even a scratch. ||82||
the persons, who are blessed by the Guru, suffer not even a scratch.
But the people whom the Gurus and pirs have (nivaajia) honoured are not touched by the heat of those thorns; meaning, they become free of vices and remove the pain of birth and death. ||82||
8TN9: Suhaavarree = pleasant, comfortable, full of comfort. Sang = with (life). Suvann = beautiful colour. Suvannarree = of beautiful colour. Deh = body.
O Farid! (The) life (of those people) is easy, and the body too is of beautiful colour (that is, free of disease),
Fareed, life is blessed and beautiful, along with the beautiful body.
Farid beauteous is the life, together with the charming body.
Sri Farid ji says: joined with a pleasant life, this body becomes fruitful.
8R5H: those whose love is with the beloved Parmatma (the 'poisonous garden' and the 'fire of pain' do not touch them; but such people) are found only rarely. ||83||
Only a rare few are found, who love their Beloved Lord. ||83||
Only few such persons are found, who love their Beloved.

But those who, having gained such a human body, have love for the beloved Parmeshvar — such saints are seen only rarely in the world. ||83|| ☬ Once the river began eating away the bank towards the town of Pakpattan. Then the people, praying for their own protection, took Farid ji there. Going up to the river, Sri Farid ji says:
RA8P: Vahan = O current! Kandhee = the river bank. Tau = you.

(The being pressed down by pains pleads before 'pain' and says:) "O current (of pains)! Do not wash away (me,) the bank (tree) (that is, do not make me suffer); you too will have to give account (of what you have done)."
O river, do not destroy your banks; you too will be asked to give your account.
O river-flood, destroy you not your bank. You too have to give an account.

"O vahan — that is, river! Do not do injustice by eating away the (kandh) bank, for going to the next world you too will have to give account." Hearing this, the river began to eat away even more; then, knowing it as defiance of Parmeshvar's command, and repenting, he says again:
Z78R: Jidhar = to which side. Rab rajaai = God's will. Tidaaoo = to that same side. Ganu kare = makes its way, goes, moves. ||84||

(The suffering person does not understand that) the flood of pains wears away only on the side where God's will is (that is, by God's will, the flood of pains comes and sweeps away the person separated from God, under the bad deeds they have done). ||84||
The river flows in whatever direction the Lord orders. ||84||
The river-flood flows in the direction, as is the will of God.

"O current — that is, O stream! Whichever way God's will is, go that way." Or: O being, do not wash away the (kandhee) bank of the bounds of the Vedas and Shastras; meaning, if you will not walk within the bounds of the Vedas, then you too must give account in the next world. For whichever way you have been commanded to go, O (vahan) being, go that way; meaning, the Vedas and Shastras are the very command of Vahiguru. ||84||
XRC8: Dukha setee = with pains, in pains. Dih = day. Soolaan = stabs, worries. Raat = (this word always has (i) at the end; it comes from the Sanskrit word 'raatri' (raatri)).
O Farid! (Because of the 'pits and mounds' formed in the mind, for beings swept along in the river of pains) the day passes in pains, and the night too passes in the stabs (of worry).
Fareed, the day passes painfully; the night is spent in anguish.
Farid! My day passes in trouble and my night in anguish.
Sri Farid ji says: the day too went with pains, and the night passed with (soolaan) — that is, with pains.
JSRM: Paatanee = boatman, ferryman. Kapar = waves, billows. Vaat = in the mouth (see salok no. 50). ||85||
The (Guru-)boatman standing (on the bank) is calling out loudly to them: "(your life's) boat (is about to fall) into the mouth of the billows (of pain)!" ||85||
The boatman stands up and shouts, "The boat is caught in the whirlpool!" ||85||
The boatman stands up and shouts, "The ship is in the midst of the whirl-pool".

So the Guru, the (paatanee) keeper of the ferry of knowledge, stands and calls out, saying: "O being! The boat of the body is falling into the (vaat) mouth of the billows of lust and the rest; so save yourself from them." ||85||
GHD2: Lammee lammee = very long. Nadee = the river of pains. Vahai = is flowing. Kerai het = to topple, to wash away.
(This) endlessly long river (of pains) is flowing to wash away the bank (trees — the worldly people) (that is, to make them suffer),
The river flows on and on; it loves to eat into its banks.
Long, the long river of life flows and if loves to eat into its banks.
O brother! The long, long river of death is flowing; or, its delight is in toppling the (kandhee) bank of good qualities.
2XYY: No = to. Kia kare = what harm can it do? Paatan = of the boatman. Paatan chet = in the boatman's mind, in the boatman's memory. Su = that boat. Chet = in memory. ||86||

(but the) whirlpool (of this river) can do no harm to (that life-)boat which stays in the mind of the (True Guru) boatman (that is, the fire of pain does not touch the person on whom the Guru keeps a glance of grace). ||86||
What can the whirlpool do to the boat, if the boatman remains alert? ||86||
What can the whirl-pool do to the boat, if the boatman remains alert?
What will the billows of lust and the rest do to the boat of the mind of that disciple for whose protection the Guru, the (paatan) boatman, stays watchful? Meaning, they can do nothing. ||86||
E3ZC: Galee = with talk, (that is,) those who please with talk. Ik = the true friend. Na lahaan = I do not find.
O Farid! There are twenty friends (to be found) who please with talk; but on searching, the true friend is not found (who would carry my life's boat across the river of pains).
Fareed, there are dozens who say they are friends; I search, but I cannot find even one.
Farid! There are twenty friends who provide lip service, however, if I search for the true friend, I find not even one.
Sri Farid ji says: friends who talk without practising are found even by the hundred, and those who practise, whom I seek — not one is found.
R185: Dhukhaan = I am smouldering within. Maaneeh = dung-cake, crumbled dry cow dung. Ma = my. Piree kaaran = for the sake of beloved friends. Tinha = those. ||87||
For want of such (sangat-)friends I am smouldering within like crumbled dung. ||87||
I yearn for my beloved like a smouldering fire. ||87||
I smoulder like cow-dung for that beloved of mine.
That is why I keep smouldering like dung; meaning, I stay in pain with worry. For I keep searching to meet those saintly friends who would lead me to my Husband. ||87||
N1F3: Bhaukna = one that has got the habit of barking, a barker. Dukheeai kaun = who should keep being troubled?

O Farid! This (my) body has become a barker (that is, it keeps demanding new things every day; for the sake of meeting its daily demands) who should keep being troubled every day? (that is, I cannot afford to keep being troubled every day).
Fareed, this body is always barking. Who can stand this constant suffering?
Farid! This body is ever barking; who can stand this continuous suffering?
Sri Farid ji says: this body is like a barking dog. Who should be in pain every day for its sake?
2ZGS: De rahaan = I will keep putting. Kitee = however much, as much as it likes. Paun = wind. ||88||
I will keep cotton plugs in my ears; let the wind blow as much as it likes (that is, let this body make as much noise of demands as it likes; I will not listen to a single one). ||88||
I have put plugs in my ears; I don't care how much the wind is blowing. ||88||
I have put stoppers in my ears. I care not how much wind is blowing.

So let us keep cotton in our ears against hearing its sounds; then let the wind blow as hard as it may. The meaning is: this body barks for clothes and the like to wear — what does it want? So let us give it food and clothing only for bare sustenance, and when it wants more, let us turn our back on it. However much it may blow the wind of craving or desire, let us not be pained by craving. ||88||
W2HP: Rab khajooree = God's dates. Maakhia = of honey. Maakhia naee = rivers of honey. Vahann = flow, are flowing.

(But what can this poor body do? To draw it, all around in the world,) O Farid, God's ripe dates (are to be seen), and rivers of honey are flowing (that is, on every side beautiful, tasty and enchanting things and sense-pleasures are present).
Fareed, God's dates have ripened, and rivers of honey flow.
Farid! God's dates have ripened and streams of honey flow.

Sri Farid ji says: God's dates have ripened, and rivers of (maakhia) honey are flowing. The meaning is: Parmeshvar's saints, the date palms, bear the fruits of good qualities, and among them, close by, flow rivers of katha and kirtan sweet as honey. That is how it is on this side.
6HGG: Deehrra = day. Hath pavanhi = hands are laid upon. Vannjai = goes, passes. ||89||
(Then again, it is also true that) every day that passes (for a person in enjoying these things) is a hand laid on their life (that is, it is going to waste). ||89||
With each passing day, your life is being stolen away. ||89||
Each day that passes steals away mortal's age.
Every (deehrra) day that (vannjai) passes without those saints lays a hand on one's lifespan; meaning, day by day life keeps decreasing. ||89||
384F: Theea = has become. Pinjar theea = has become a handful of bones. Khoondahi = are pecking. Kaag = crows, vices, the cravings for worldly things.

O Farid! (This barking) body has become very thin (by falling into sense-pleasures and vices); it is left a handful of bones. (Still) these crows keep pecking at its palms (that is, cravings for worldly things and sense-pleasures keep stabbing its mind).
Fareed, my withered body has become a skeleton; the crows are pecking at my palms.
Farid! My aged frail body has become a skeleton and the crows peck at my palms.

Sri Farid ji says: I have done such austerities that the body has dried up like a skeleton, and, as on a corpse, crows peck at the soles of the feet. Or: vices such as lust and anger, like crows, peck at and pull on the palms of the senses.
RK2Z: Ajai = even now (when the body has lost even its strength from enjoying the world's pleasures). Na baahurrio = has not been pleased, has not shown mercy. ||90||

See, the fate of a person (caught in vices) is strange indeed: even now (when their body has lost even its strength from enjoying the world's pleasures) God has not been pleased with them (that is, their longing has not ended). ||90||
Even now, God has not come to help me; behold, this is the fate of all mortal beings. ||90||
Even till now, God has not come to my aid, see you, that such is the fate of the man.
So even by doing such austerities, God has not yet come to me. From this, see, brother, how ill-fated I, a servant, am. ||90|| ☬ Hanging in the well in austerity, he says to a crow:
L253: Kaaga = the crows, the vices, the cravings for worldly things. Karang = skeleton, a body grown very thin. Sagla = all.

The crows have picked over even the skeleton and eaten all the flesh (that is, cravings for worldly things and sense-pleasures keep stabbing even this utterly wasted body; they have drawn all the strength out of this barking body).
The crows have searched my skeleton, and eaten all my flesh.
The crows have searched my skeleton and eaten up all flesh.
O crow! You have searched out — that is, hunted all over — my (karang) carcass and eaten all my flesh.
0568: Mat chhuhau = God forbid anyone touch them (see the words 'bhijau', 'varsau' and 'tutau' in salok no. 25). Aas = longing. ||91||
God forbid any vice touch (my) eyes; in them let the longing to see the beloved Prabhu stay settled. ||91||
But please do not touch these eyes; I hope to see my Lord. ||91||
O crows! Touch you not these two eyes, as I hope to behold my Beloved.

But do not touch these two eyes, for I hope to see with these eyes the Husband in His form with attributes. Or: O crow of death, searcher of the carcasses of bodies, you have eaten all my flesh of good qualities. But do not touch these two, the mind and the intellect, for I hope to see with these eyes the Husband in His attributeless form. ||91||
P9NW: Kaaga = O crow! O craving for worldly things! Choond na = do not peck. Pinjara = the dried-up body. Basai = (if it is) in your power, if you can. Ta = then.
O crow! Do not peck at my skeleton; if (this) is in your power, then fly away (from here),
O crow, do not peck at my skeleton; if you have landed on it, fly away.
O Crow, corrode you not my skeleton. If you have perched upon it, then fly you away.
O crow! Do not peck at this cage of the body; even if you have settled on it, fly away from here.
HQPS: Jit = in which. Jit pinjarai = in which body. Tidoo = out of that body. ||92||

do not eat the flesh from this body in which my Husband-Prabhu dwells (that is, O craving for sense-objects, stop stabbing this body of mine; have mercy, go, and set it free. In this body dwells the love of the Husband-Prabhu; do not try to push it towards sense-pleasures). ||92||
Do not eat the flesh from that skeleton, within which my Husband Lord abides. ||92||
The skeleton, in which dwells my spouse, eat you not flesh therefrom.
For do not eat flesh from that cage in which my (sahu) Husband, Parmeshvar, dwells. ||92||
KMYC: Nimaanee = poor, humble. Sad = call, summons. Sad kare = is calling. Nighria = O homeless being! Ghar = in the house.
O Farid! The poor grave is calling (to the person, and saying): "O homeless being! Come into (your own) home;
Fareed, the poor grave calls out, "O homeless one, come back to your home.
Farid! The poor grave calls out, "O homeless come to your Home".
Sri Farid ji says: the (gor) grave, which is (nimaanee) lowly, is (sad) calling to the soul: "O homeless one! I, who am your home — come here.
87MQ: Sarpar = in the end. Maithai = to me. ||93||
(that is,) in the end (you) must come to me alone; (then) do not fear death (so much)." ||93||
You shall surely have to come to me; do not be afraid of death." ||93||
You shall assuredly come to me, so fear not your death.
(Sarpar) in the end your coming must be to me alone; so do not bring the fear of dying into your heart." ||93||
MC3C: Loin = eyes. Inhee loinee = with these eyes (under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'). Ketee = so many (creatures), endless beings.
While these eyes looked on (that is, before my eyes), so many creatures have gone (have fallen prey to death).
These eyes have seen a great many leave.
Within the sight of these eyes of mine good many have departed.
While these eyes were looking, how much of creation has gone!
QJ8Q: O Farid! (Even seeing creation going away,) everyone thinks only of their own self-interest (that is, every being is in the pursuit of the world); I too am caught in worry about my own. ||94||
Fareed, the people have their fate, and I have mine. ||94||
Farid! People have their own anxieties and I have my own.
Sri Farid ji says: all people have their own worries; my own worry has come upon me. ||94|| ☬ A voice from the sky came to Farid ji; that is what he says:
1BXW: If you set yourself right, you will meet Me, and only in being joined to Me will you find comfort (not in the things of the world).
God says, "If you reform yourself, you shall meet me, and meeting me, you shall be at peace.
Says the Lord, "If O man, you reform yourself, you shall meet me.
If you set yourself right, then you will meet Me; and when I have met you, then you will have comfort.
SNQS: O Farid! If you become Mine (that is, give up love for the world and begin to love Me, then) the whole world will become yours (that is, Maya will run after you). ||95||
O Fareed, if you will be mine, the whole world will be yours." ||95||
and if you belong to me, the whole world shall belong to you", says Farid.
So, O Farid, if you stay My servant, then the whole world will become your servant. ||95|| ☬ He gives two illustrations of the impermanence of the body:
1TQD: Kandhee = bank. Rukhrra = a little tree, a poor tree. Dheer = patience, reassurance.
How long will the poor tree (growing) on the bank (of a river) keep up its hope? O Farid! How long can water be kept in an unbaked pot?
How long can the tree remain implanted on the river-bank?
How long can the tree remain stable on the river-bank?
How much (cheer) of mind can the (rukhrra) tree on the (kandhee) bank of a river hold? That is, none at all.
YFWN: (In the same way, a person stands on the bank of the river of death; the breaths in this body are running out). ||96||
Fareed, how long can water be kept in a soft clay pot? ||96||
Farid! For how long, can the water be kept in unbaked earthen vessel?

And how long will water be kept in an unbaked pot? That is, it cannot stay at all. The meaning is: just as a tree cannot stay on the bank, and just as water does not stay in an unbaked pot, such is this body's staying in the world; so this life in the world is momentary. ||96||
ZC1Z: Mahal = brick houses. Nisakhan = quite empty, deserted. Tal = below, down in the earth.
O Farid! (When death comes,) the mansions are left empty; one has to make one's dwelling below the earth (in the grave).
Fareed, the mansions are vacant; those who lived in them have gone to live underground.
Farid! The mansions have been emptied and their occupants have gone to abide below the earth (in the graves).
Sri Farid ji says: brother, on dying, the (mahal) mansions are left (nisakhan) utterly empty, and the body's dwelling comes (tal) below the earth — that is, in the place of the grave.

J20T: Bahsan = will sit. Goraan nimaaneea = these graves which people shun. Mal = occupying.
In those graves that people shun, souls will go and sit for ever.
They remain there, in those unhonored graves.
Those unhonoured graves shall be taken possession of by the souls.
The souls, which are humble, have (mal) occupied — that is, taken up — the places of the graves.
ZWLN: O Sheikh (Farid)! Worship (God); today or tomorrow you must set out (from these mansions). ||97||
O Shaykh, dedicate yourself to God; you will have to depart, today or tomorrow. ||97||
You recite Lord's Name, as you shall depart today or tomorrow (sooner or later).
So Sheikh Farid ji says: O brother! Speak of worship — that is, worship — for today or tomorrow you must leave this world. ||97||
S5KD: Evai = thus, like this. Dhaaha = bank, edge.
O Farid! Just as there is the bank of a river (which is crumbling with the force of the water), so is the bank of the river of death (into which endless beings keep falling as their lives run out).
Fareed, the shore of death looks like the river-bank, being eroded away.
The shore of death looks like the eroded bank of a river.

Sri Farid ji says: the edge of death appears like a river eating away its bank; meaning, such is the dying of beings that one sees. Or: just as those sitting in a boat do not notice the boat moving and only know it when it reaches the bank, so a being does not notice the body changing; it is known only when the time of death has come.
ZR6A: Hool = uproar. Kaahaaha = wailing. Dojak = hell.
(Beyond death,) on the far side, blazing hells are spoken of (for the wrongdoers); there their wailing and uproar is going on.
Beyond is the burning hell, from which cries and shrieks are heard.
Beyond is the burning hell where the cries of shrieks and wailings are heard there.
Ahead, in the next world, (dojak) hell is heard to be blazing with fire, in which the (kaahaaha) cries of sinful beings in (hool) pain are rising.
69ET: Ik = many beings (the word 'ik[i]' is the plural of the word 'ik').
Some (fortunate ones) have come to full understanding (of how to live life here, but) some are going about carelessly.
Some understand this completely, while others wander around carelessly.
Some understand it fully while some still wander about heedlessly.
Some people of the sangat have come to full understanding, and some, without understanding, go about careless.
V67C: The deeds one does here in the world become witnesses (to one's life) in God's court. ||98||
Those actions which are done in this world, shall be examined in the Court of the Lord. ||98||
The deeds, which man does in the world, they bear witness in the Lord's Court.
But whatever (amal) deeds beings have done in the world — those very deeds will be witnesses in the next world. ||98||
F531: O Farid! (A person is absorbed in the shows and spectacles of the world, just as) a heron sitting on the bank of a river frolics.
Fareed, the crane perches on the river bank, playing joyfully.
Farid! Sitting on the river-bank, the crane joyfully sports.
Sri Farid ji says: just as a heron, sitting by the (kannai) side of a river, is (kel) at play —
PGE5: Kel = play. Hanjh = swan (a heron white as a swan). Achinte = suddenly. Tihu = that (heron).
(Just as on that) swan (-white heron), while it frolics, hawks suddenly swoop, (so the messengers of death come and seize a person).
While it is playing, a hawk suddenly pounces on it.
While the crane is engaged in sport, the hawk pounces upon it unexpectedly.
on that (hanjh) heron, while it plays, a hawk (achinte) suddenly swoops. The meaning: in the same way, while this being enjoys many pleasures, the messengers of Yama have come and struck it down.
8DBQ: When the hawks swoop on it, it forgets all its frolics (it has to think of its own life; such is a person's state when death comes).
When the Hawk of God attacks, playful sport is forgotten.
Yea, when the hawk of that God strikes, it forgets the sports.
When that hawk, Yama, swoops, this being, the heron, forgets all its (kelaan) talk of enjoying pleasures.
59TN: Man = in the mind. Chete san = were in memory, were remembered. Gaalee = things. ||99||
God did the things that were never in (a person's) mind or thought. ||99||
God does what is not expected or even considered. ||99||
What was not even remotely contemplated in his mind even those things, the Lord has manifest.
The things that were not (chete) remembered in this being's mind and thought — those Vahiguru has done. The meaning is: beings did not remember dying, and that very thing surely happened. ||99||
JG0A: Dehuree = beautiful body, well-fed body. Chalai = goes on, keeps working. Ann = with grain.
(A person's) well-fed body of three and a half maunds keeps working on the strength of water and grain.
The body is nourished by water and grain.
The body of three and a half maunds, lives on water and grain.
Sri Farid ji says: this body's (man) measure, by one's own hands, is only three and a half cubits, and it goes on through water and grain; meaning, it is sustained by them.
DWVW: Vich = (this always has (i) at the end; the word 'bin' always has (u) at the end). Vat = again and again. Aasoonee = a little hope, a pretty hope. Bannh = tying.
A person comes into the world tying some pretty hope (but the hope is not fulfilled).
The mortal comes into the world with high hopes.
Entertaining high hopes, the mortal had come into the world.
For this servant came into this world to worship, and then goes about bound by many (aasoonee) hopes.
52SQ: Malak = angel. Al = of. Malkal maut = the angel of death.
When the angel of death comes, breaking all the doors (of the body) (that is, making all the senses useless),
But when the Messenger of Death comes, it breaks down all the doors.
However, when the Death's myrmidon comes he breaks open all the doors.
But when death, the (malkal) crusher, comes, it will break all the doors of the senses. The senses will grow slack; meaning, no door can hold it back.
E9LV: those beloved brothers (of the person) tie them up and send them off ahead (with the angel of death).
It binds and gags the mortal, before the eyes of his beloved brothers.
He binds down the mortal, before the very eyes of those dear brothers of his.
Those beloved brothers who raised one, and in whose company one found joy, have tied one up, laid one on a cot or a bier, put it on men's heads and sent it ahead, while they themselves walk behind.
E7GT: See! The person has set off on the shoulders of four men.
Behold, the mortal being is going away, carried on the shoulders of four men.
See! The mortal (his dead body) is going on the shoulders of four men.
O brother, look! The body of that servant, that being, goes along on the (kannhi) shoulders of four men.
C2M7: Aae kamm = came to use, were of help. ||100||
O Farid! In the court (of Parmatma) only those (good) deeds are of help that are done (while living) in the world. ||100||
Fareed, only those good deeds done in the world will be of any use in the Court of the Lord. ||100||
Farid! Only the good deeds, which he did in the world, would be of avail to him in the Lord's Court.
Sri Farid ji says: whatever (amal) deeds, good or bad, the being did in the world — those very deeds came to use in the court; so, O being, love good deeds and worship. ||100||
4BC4: Hau = I. Balihaaree = a sacrifice, devoted. Tinh = under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'. Jangal = in the forest. Vaas = dwelling, residence.
O Farid! I am a sacrifice to those birds whose dwelling is in the forest,
Fareed, I am a sacrifice to those birds which live in the jungle.
Farid! I am a sacrifice to those birds that live in the woods.
Sri Farid ji says: those whose dwelling is in the forests — that is, the saints who live in the woods — to those saintly birds I am a sacrifice.
SX5V: Kakar = pebbles, gravel. Thal = on the ground, on the earth. Rab paas = God's side, God's support. Chhorranhi = (under the letter 'n' there is a half 'h'). ||101||

who peck at pebbles, live on the ground, (yet) do not leave God's support (that is, better than the well-fed person living in mansions who forgets God are those birds who make nests in trees and get by pecking at pebbles, yet keep God in mind). ||101||
They peck at the roots and live on the ground, but they do not leave the Lord's side. ||101||
For, they peck at roots, live on the ground and leave not the Lord's side.

The saints who, living in the (bal) [sic: 'thal'] places of the forest, (chugan) eat (kakar) pebbles and such — that is, roots and tubers — and do not leave God's side; meaning, doing austerities, they always keep remembering Parmeshvar. ||101||
KR03: Phiree = has changed. Van = forest (that is, the forest tree). (Note the difference between the form of the word 'van' and the grammatical form of the word 'van[i]' in saloks no. 19 and 43).
O Farid! The season has changed, the forest (every plant in it) has shaken, the leaves are falling.
Fareed, the seasons change, the woods shake and the leaves drop from the trees.
Farid! The season has changed, the woods shake and the leaves continually drop off.

Sri Farid ji says: when the season of youth turned and old age came, then the forest of the body began to tremble, the leaves of the teeth fell, and the senses became ready to fall; meaning, all the limbs grew slack.
A2PM: I have searched all four directions (of the world); there is no permanence anywhere (neither can the season stay the same, nor can trees and their leaves stay for ever. That is, as time passes, old age comes upon a person, all the limbs grow weak, and at last they leave the world). ||102||
I have searched in the four directions, but I have not found any resting place anywhere. ||102||
I have searched the four directions and have not found a stable abode anywhere.
So, O brother, I have searched the four directions — that is, looked with my eyes; with this body one does not get to stay in any place. ||102||
SK6V: Paarr = tearing. Patola = a silk cloth (worn over the head by a woman). Dhaj = rags. Kambalrree = a poor little blanket.
O Farid! Let me tear my silk cloth into rags and put on a poor little blanket.
Fareed, I have torn my clothes to tatters; now I wear only a rough blanket.
Farid! Tearing off all my robes into tatters, I just wear a blanket.
Sri Farid ji says: let me tear my (patola) clothes and make a (dhaj) flag or a fakir's robe, and wear a blanket on my body.
E91R: Jinhee vesee = by which garbs. Sahu = Husband. ||103||
Let me put on those very garbs by which (my) Husband, Parmatma, may be met. ||103||

O friend! For what do you tear your (patola) clothes, and why do you wear a blanket? Meaning: why give up the household and take on a fakir's garb?
8HT0: Ghar hee = {ghar[i] hee. The (i) of the word 'ghar[i]' has dropped because of the adverb 'hee'} in the house itself. Raas = good, clean. ||104||

7GUD: Garab = pride. Vadiaaeea garab = pride in greatness, pride in worldly honour. Dhan = because of wealth. Joban = because of youth. Aagaah = boundless.
O Farid! Those people who had pride in worldly honour, (some) pride because of boundless wealth or because of youth,
Fareed, those who are very proud of their greatness, wealth and youth,
Farid! They, who greatly pride on their greatness, wealth and youth;
Sri Farid ji says: those who have (aagaah) great pride in greatnesses such as wealth and youth —
PKCH: Dhanee = God, Parmatma. Siu = from. Meehaahu = after the rain. ||105||

shall return empty-handed from their Lord, like sandhills after the rain. ||105||
they come empty-handed from their Master, like a mound after the rain.

Those people go from the world empty of the attainment of (dhanee) Parmeshvar. Just as, when rain falls, the (tibe) high places stay empty of water; meaning, good qualities do not settle in the proud. ||105||
6NAA: O Farid! Those people who have forgotten Parmatma's Name — their faces look frightening (one feels fear at the sight of them, whether they wear silk, or have wealth, or youth, or honour and greatness).
Fareed, the faces of those who forget the Lord's Name are dreadful.
Farid! dreadful are the faces of those who forget the Lord's Name.
Sri Farid ji says: those who have forgotten Vahiguru's Name — the faces of those people are (daraavane) fearsome.
3NNV: Aithai = in this life. Ghanereea = many, great. Thaur na thaau = neither place nor shelter. ||106||
(As long as) they are here (living), many pains befall them, and further on too they find no place or shelter (that is, they are only pushed about). ||106||
They suffer terrible pain here, and hereafter they find no place of rest or refuge. ||106||
Here, they undergo many troubles and, hereafter, find no abode and refuge.
In (aithai) this world too they have many pains, and further on, in the next world, they find no good place to stay. ||106||
WZ1C: Pichhal raat = in the last part of the night, at the amrit vela. Na jaagiohi = you did not wake. Muiohi = you died.
O Farid! If you did not wake at the amrit vela, then (this ugly life is such that) you are dead while still alive.
Fareed, if you do not awaken in the early hours before dawn, you are dead while yet alive.
Farid! If you wake not in the closing hours of the night, you are like dead even while alive.

Sri Farid ji says: the one who did not wake in the last part of the night — that is, did not give up sleep at that time and worship — that person has died while still alive. The meaning is: at that nectar time, because there is no noise, the mind becomes one-pointed.
L1KG: If you have forgotten God, God has not forgotten you (that is, Parmatma is watching your deeds at every moment). ||107||
Although you have forgotten God, God has not forgotten you. ||107||
Although you have forgotten your Lord, even then, the Lord has forgotten you not.

O brother! Even if you have forgotten God, you have not been forgotten by God; meaning, He gives you every comfort. As it is said: 'The Compassionate to the lowly, the treasure of mercy, sees our faults yet never tires of giving.' ||107||
2SYK: Kant = Husband, Parmatma. Rangaavla = (see 'rangaavalee' in salok no. 82) full of beauty, beautiful.
O Farid! The Husband (Parmatma) is beautiful and greatly free of need.
Fareed, my Husband Lord is full of joy; He is Great and Self-sufficient.
Farid! Mirthful is my Spouse, He is altogether care-free.
Sri Farid ji says: our Husband, Parmeshvar, (rangaavla) full of bliss, is greater than all, and free of need; meaning, He is subject to no one.
KQRT: Alah setee = with God. Saaj = make, form. Sachaavaan = belonging to the True One, belonging to Parmatma. Ehu saaj = this form, (that is,) the 'beautiful' and 'need-free' form. ||108||

(Rising at the amrit vela,) if we are dyed with God, then (a person too) receives this (beautiful and need-free) form that belongs to God (that is, a person's mind becomes beautiful, and they no longer depend on anyone). ||108||
To be imbued with the Lord God - this is the most beautiful decoration. ||108||
To be imbued with the Lord; this alone is the most befitting decoration.
To stay dyed with that (alah) Vahiguru — that is, to love Him — this alone is the true means of attaining that Husband. ||108||
6Z4M: Ik kar = make the same, know as one. Vikaar = sin. Te = from.
O Farid! (Through the practice of remembering God on rising at the amrit vela,) know the pain and pleasure (that come in life) as one and the same; put sin out of your heart,
Fareed, look upon pleasure and pain as the same; eradicate corruption from your heart.
Farid deem you pain and pleasure as the same and banish sin from your mind.
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Know pain and pleasure as one, and put vices out of the mind.
EE7K: Alah bhaavai = (what) pleases God. Darbaar = God's court. ||109||
Know as good whatever happens in God's will; then you will attain the court (of Parmatma). ||109||
Whatever pleases the Lord God is good; understand this, and you will reach His Court. ||109||
Whatever pleases God, that alone is good. Then alone shall you attain to His Court.
Whatever pleases that (alah) unseeable Vahiguru, know that as good; then you will attain His court. ||109||
XWXY: Dunee = the world, the people of the world. Vajaaee = driven by Maya. Naal = along with the world.
O Farid! The people of the world (are instruments) playing as (Maya) plays them; you too are playing along with them (that is, dancing as Maya makes you dance).
Fareed, the world dances as it dances, and you dance with it as well.
Farid! The world dances as the devil makes it dance and you too are playing with it;

Sri Guru ji says through Sri Farid ji: the (dunee) creation plays as ignorance plays it — that is, makes every kind of movement — and you too play along with the people of that world; meaning, you act as they do, with ignorance.
7KSX: Jis = whose. Saar = care. Alahu = Parmatma. ||110||

Only that (fortunate) being does not play (as Maya plays it) whose care (protection) Parmatma Himself takes (so rise at the amrit vela and join in His remembrance, so that you too may be cared for). ||110||
That soul alone does not dance with it, who is under the care of the Lord God. ||110||
that person alone dances not, who is under the Lord's care.

O mind! The one whom He Himself, the unseeable or pure in form, takes care of — that is, keeps as His own — that being does not act according to ignorance, but acts according to the scriptures. ||110||
F4TB: Rata = dyed. Dunee = the world, Maya. Kitai kamm = of any use (it does not come).
O Farid! (Rising at the amrit vela is not enough; what is the gain in rising if even then) the heart stays dyed with (the things of) the world? The world is of no use (at the end).
Fareed, the heart is imbued with this world, but the world is of no use to it at all.
Farid! The mind is imbued with this world, but the world is of no avail.
Sri Farid ji says: the Maya with which this being's (dil) mind is dyed is of no use to it at all.

0JEN: Misal phakeeraan = the way of living of fakirs. Gaakhree = hard. Poor karamm = through full good fortune. ||111||
(Rising and remembering God,) this way of living of fakirs is very hard, and it is gained only through great good fortune. ||111||
It is so difficult to be like the fakeers - the Holy Saints; it is only achieved by perfect karma. ||111||
Difficult it is to be like the saints. That position is obtained only through perfect deeds.
The (misal) way of life of fakirs is (gaakhree) hard, and it is attained through complete good deeds. ||111||

The first watch of the night brings flowers, and the later watches of the night bring fruit.
The Lord's meditation in its first watch yields flowers, while the latter watches of the night, yield the fruits as well.
Waking in the first watch of the night is like a flower, and waking in the last watch of the night is like the fruit.
X9T8: Jaagannhi = under the letter 'n' there is an 'h'. Lahann = obtain. Kanno = from (see the word 'kannai' in salok no. 99). ||112||
Those people who wake (at the amrit vela) receive the gift from Parmatma. ||112||
Those who remain awake and aware, receive the gifts from the Lord. ||112||
They, who remain awake, obtain gifts from the Lord.
Those who wake at that time — those very people receive from the Master the gift of good qualities. ||112||
UDRN: Daatee = gifts. Sandeea = of. Tis naal = with that (Master). Kia chalai = what power can prevail.
The gifts belong to the Master (Himself). What power can (anyone) have against that Master?
The gifts are from our Lord and Master; who can force Him to bestow them?
All bounties are of the Lord; however, who can force Him to grant them?
The gifts are the Master's; what power can anyone have against Him?
D59J: Ik = many people. Lahanhi = obtain. ❀ Note: the word 'daat' ends in (i); its plural is formed by lengthening the (i); in the same way from the word 'lahar' (ending in (i)) comes 'laharee', as in 'saair laharee dei'. ||113||

Some, though awake (at the amrit vela), do not receive (these gifts); some (fortunate ones) He Himself wakes while they sleep (that is, some, though awake at the amrit vela, stay asleep in Maya in the form of ego and the like; and to some heedless ones He Himself, by His grace, gives understanding). ||113||
Some are awake, and do not receive them, while He awakens others from sleep to bless them. ||113||
Some, who are awake, receive them not, while, some He Himself wakes from sleep and blesses them with gifts.

Some — pandits and the like — though awake, do not receive; and some, while asleep, He wakes and gives to. The meaning is: by His grace He gives knowledge and other qualities to the unlettered. ||113||
5HDW: Koo = to. Tau tan = in your body, within you. Kor = flaw, lack. Kaaee = some.
O (soul-bride) searching for the Husband (Parmatma)! (You rise at the amrit vela and worship to meet the Husband, Parmatma, yet you have still not met Him) — there is some flaw within you yourself.
You search for your Husband Lord; you must have some fault in your body.
You, who is searching for your Groom, must have some fault in the body.
O soul-bride! You who search for the happy wedlock of Parmeshvar the Husband — there is some (kor) defect or fault in your body.
21B8: Those whose name is 'happy wives' have no other reliance within them (that is, the gift of union with the Husband is given only to those who do not stake any 'claim' for rising at the amrit vela). ||114||
Those who are known as happy soul-brides, do not look to others. ||114||
They, who are called chaste brides, cherish not hope of another.
The saints whose name is 'happy wives' do not look to any other god. ||114||

If there is this bow of patience in the mind, if patience itself is the bow's string,
Within yourself, make patience the bow, and make patience the bowstring.
In your mind, make patience a bow, and patience a bow string,
Sri Farid ji says: O brother! Those people who make (sabar) contentment the bow in the heart, and then make this body of patience the (neehano) string of that bow —
E7GV: Sanda = of. Baan = arrow. Khata na karee = does not let it go to waste, does not let it miss. ||115||
(and) the arrow too is of patience, then Parmatma does not let it miss (its mark). ||115||
Make patience the arrow, the Creator will not let you miss the target. ||115||
and patience yours arrows; thus, the Creator will not allow you to miss the mark.

those who have made the patience of speech their arrow — the arrow of patience they have shot, that is, the word they have spoken, (khaalak) Parmeshvar does not make (khata) futile; meaning, all the doings of the contented bear fruit. ||115||
42B6: Saabaree = people of patience. Evai = in this way, (that is,) in patience itself. Tan jaalenhi = burn the body, toil (that is, while the world sleeps, they rise at the amrit vela and worship, and make firm the lessons of freedom from need, turning away from sin, and acceptance of the Will).
People of patience, staying in patience, toil at worship in this very way (always in patience),

The men of patience abide in patience. Thiswise, burn they their body's ego.
Sri Farid ji says: those (saabaree) contented people burn their bodies in this way within contentment itself; meaning, they pass their lives in contentment.

G1FJ: Suaau = purpose, aim, the goal of life. Banda = O servant! O person! Dirr = firm.

This patience is the aim of life, if somehow you implant it in your mind, O man.
So this is the (suaau) gain of that contentment: if you, becoming a (banda) servant, hold contentment firmly in mind,
R1H4: Vadh = growing. Theevahi = you will become. Vaahrra = a little stream. Tut = shrinking, lessening. ||117||

then you will grow and become a river, (and) will not shrink into a little stream (that is, by making a life of patience, your heart will grow into a river; love for the whole world will arise in your heart; no narrow-heartedness will be left within you). ||117||

then you will grow and become a river, and will not then shrink into a (vaahrra) stream; meaning, having become certain that your own self is the form of Brahm, you will never again take on the sense of being a separate jiva. ||117||

My body is heated like an oven and my bones burn like fire-wood.
Let this body of mine burn like a (tanoor) oven — that is, let me do austerities as hard as the five fires and the like — and let the bones too, in place of firewood, burn up.

(On the path to meeting the beloved God, if I) grow tired (walking) on my feet, then let me walk on my head. Were my feet to tire, I would walk on my head, if I can meet with my Beloved.
Walking on foot for pilgrimage, when I grow tired, let me (julaan) walk on my head — if only, somehow, I might meet the (piree) Husband. ||119|| ☬ Sri Guru, the Third Patshahi, utters:
6G4L: Do not burn the body like an oven (with fires); and do not burn the bones as if they were firewood.
Do not heat up your body like an oven, and do not burn your bones like firewood.
Heat you not your body like an oven and burn not your bones like fire-wood.
O brother! Do not heat this body like an oven, and do not burn the bones in place of firewood; meaning, do not do such austerity of tamas.
TZR2: Sir = the head. Pairee = the feet. Pherria = has spoiled. Nihaal = see, behold. ||120||

What harm have yours head and feet done you? See your Love within you.
What have the head and feet and the other limbs (pherria) spoiled for you? So (nihaal) see the (piree) Beloved, Parmeshvar, within your heart. ||120||
PA8D: Maidde naal = with me, in my heart.

I search for my Friend, but my Friend is already with me.
I go searching for my Friend, however, my Friend is ever with me.
The one who befriends, whom I am searching for — that Friend, Vahiguru, is right with me.
U6GA: Alakh = without marks, the One whose special mark cannot be known. Dei dikhaal = shows. ||121||
O Nanak! That (Friend) has no marks; He cannot be recognised (by a being through their own effort); the True Guru shows Him. ||121||
O Nanak, the Unseen Lord cannot be seen; He is revealed only to the Gurmukh. ||121||
Nanak, the Unseen Lord is seen not; the Exalted Guru shows Him to the mortal.
Sri Guru ji says: that unseeable form, which cannot be perceived by mind or speech — the True Guru, who is the chief form of all, shows Him at once. ||121||
VAYW: Seeing the swans swimming, the herons too grew eager,
Seeing the swans swimming, the cranes became excited.
Seeing the swans swimming, the cranes too were enthused.

Just as, seeing the swans swim, the herons too grew eager to swim, so, seeing the saints swim across the world, the hypocrites too were stirred; meaning, those hypocrites were eager to have themselves worshipped like the saints.
P6JD: but the poor herons (in this attempt) drowned and died, head down and feet up. ||122||
The poor cranes were drowned to death, with their heads below the water and their feet sticking out above. ||122||
The poor cranes were drowned to death with their heads below and their feet above.
Those (bapurre) poor hypocrite-herons have drowned and died in the hells, or in the womb itself; their heads went down and their feet up; meaning, they wander through births. ||122||
Q3R7: Vadhans = a great swan. Sang = companionship.
I thought this was some great swan; that is why I kept its company.
I knew him as a great swan, so I associated with him.
I deemed him to be a great Swan, therefore, I associated with him,
When I knew this body to be excellent, like a swan, then I loved it.
58AQ: Je jaana = if I had known. Janam = in this birth, all one's life. Na bherree = would not touch. ||123||
But if I had known that this was a worthless heron, I would never have gone near it. ||123||
If I had known that he was a only wretched crane, I would never in my life have crossed paths with him. ||123||
If I had known, that this was only a wretched crane, I would not have touched him with my limb from the beginning.

And if I had known that this was a poor heron — that is, worthless — I would not have (bherree) joined my heart with it from birth to the end. ☬ Or: in these two saloks there is a dialogue between Farid ji and a herdsman. Seeing Farid ji hanging in a well by an iron chain, the herdsman himself hung in the well by a rope of grass. Then Farid ji, in the pride of his own austerity, called him a heron and called himself a swan. Then the herdsman said: "I too thought that Farid ji was a saint like a swan, and so I kept your company. If I had taken you for just a poor heron — that is, known you to be a hypocrite — I would not have joined my limbs with yours as long as I lived." ||123|| ☬ Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, standing impartial, removes the pride of both:
MLZS: Kia = whether. Ja kau = on whom. Nadar = glance of grace.
Whether a swan or a heron — the one on whom (Prabhu) casts His glance of grace (He makes His own; so why hate anyone?)
Who is a swan, and who is a crane, if God blesses him with His Glance of Grace?
What does it matter, whether, he, on whom God casts His merciful glance, is a swan or a crane?
What is a swan and what is a heron — that is, what is high and what is low — whoever Vahiguru looks upon with grace.
LEEG: Tis = to that (Prabhu). Kaagahu = from a crow. ||124||
O Nanak! If it pleases Parmatma, He makes (never mind a heron) a swan even out of a crow (that is, He reforms even a great wrongdoer). ||124||
If it pleases Him, O Nanak, He changes a crow into a swan. ||124||
If it pleases Him, O Nanak, He changes a crow into a swan.
Sri Guru ji says: if it pleases that Master, He turns the crow-like into an excellent saint, as happened with Ajamal, Valmik and others. ||124||
2YM7: Sarvar = of the pool (of the world). Hekrro = alone.

There is only one bird in the lake, but there are fifty trappers.
In the lake there is but one bird, however, there are fifty snarers.

In the pool of the world there is (hekrre) one soul-bird. Those who would snare it are the ten senses and the four inner faculties — 14; their objects, also 14; their presiding gods, 14; the vices such as lust, which are five — 5; and the three gunas. These are the fifty strong ones.
PQ4F: Gad thia = has got stuck. Laharee = in the waves. ||125||

This body (of mine) has got stuck in the waves (of vice in the pool of the world). O True (Prabhu)! (To escape them) I have hope only in You (Your help) (so if austerities must be done to meet You, even that is a cheap bargain). ||125||
This body is caught in the waves of desire. O my True Lord, You are my only hope! ||125||
This body is caught in the waves of desires. O True Lord, my hope is in You alone.

And this subtle body — that is, the mind — has got (gad) stuck in the waves of thoughts; meaning, it is entangled. So, O true Vahiguru, to escape them my hope is in You alone; meaning, You alone are the one who saves from these vices. ||125|| ☬ A seeker-friend says to one of knowledge:
3QZ3: (O sister!) What is that word? What is that virtue? What is that supreme mantra?

What is that word, what is that virtue and what is that jewel-like spell?

1PRK: If you put on these three garbs, then (my) Husband will come under (your) control. ||127||
Wear these three robes, O sister, and you will captivate your Husband Lord. ||127||

ZBM3: who, though having strength, lives like the weak (that is, forces no one),
if you are powerful, be weak;
be powerless, even when blessed with power,
who, though having (taan) strength, stays like the weak —

who, when they have nothing at all to give, shares out their very self (that is, their own portion),

and shares with others, even when there is almost naught to share;

who, when they have no goods of their own and something comes, still shares it and then eats. Or: the self — that is, the ego — which is in truth non-existent, they (vandaae) put away; meaning, they become free of ego.
FUP0: some such person alone should be called a devotee. ||128||
How rare is one who is known as such a devotee. ||128||
only some such a rare one is called a saint.
Whoever is like this, let them call themselves a devotee. ||128||
NX2C: Gaalaai = speak. Ik = even one word. Dhanee = Master, Husband.
Do not speak even one harsh word (because) the true Master (is dwelling) in all.
Do not utter even a single harsh word; your True Lord and Master abides in all.
Recite you not even a single harsh word, since your True Master abides among all,
O brother! Do not (gaalaai) speak even one harsh word to anyone, for the true Master, Vahiguru, pervades all beings.
0UJD: Hiaau = heart. Kaihee = of anyone. Thaah = break. Maanak = pearls. ||129||
Do not hurt anyone's heart (because) all these (beings) are priceless pearls. ||129||
Do not break anyone's heart; these are all priceless jewels. ||129||
Break you not any one's heart as invaluable are all these jewels.
So do not break anyone's (hiaau) heart, for in the heart of every being Parmeshvar abides as a priceless jewel; or, everyone's heart is a priceless jewel. ||129||
P9ZH: Thaahan = breaking, hurting. Mool = at all. Machaangva = not good.
The minds of all beings are pearls; hurting (anyone) is not good at all.
The minds of all are like precious jewels; to harm them is not good at all.
Precious like jewels are the minds of all. To hurt them is not at all good.
The mind of every being is a jewel; so breaking — that is, hurting — that heart is not at all (machaangva) good; meaning, it is bad.
0N6X: If you long to meet the beloved Prabhu, then do not break anyone's heart. ||130||
If you desire your Beloved, then do not break anyone's heart. ||130||
If you desire your Beloved, then do not hurt any one's heart.

O brother! If you have, from every side and especially, a (sik) longing for Parmeshvar the Husband, then do not break anyone's heart. ||130|| ☬ Once, in Brahmlok, Brahma ji was seated with the Vedas in the assembly of the gods. At that time Sri Vishnu Dev ji came. All the gods stood up to honour him, but Brahma ji, with the Vedas, held to pride and did not honour him. Then Vishnu ji, angered, cursed them: "You have not kept the proper order because of your pride; so go to the mortal world, take human form, and be without knowledge." Hearing the curse, Brahma ji with the Vedas then bowed to Vishnu ji, asked when the curse would end, and sought forgiveness for their offence. Then Hari ji said: "Let each Veda take four forms, and with Brahma make seventeen forms, and be born in the Bhatt line of Brahmins. When in the Kali age I take the incarnation named Sri Guru Nanak, and the fifth incarnation is named Sri Guru Arjan ji, then you will meet me and utter praise, and then, having become knowledge itself, you will come back here."
