Hearing these words of Bhagvant, they took seventeen forms in the mortal world, and Brahma ji's name was Bhikha. All seventeen together, many ...

SNML: Akal Purakh is One, whose Name is 'the One who Is', who is the Creator of creation, who pervades all, who is without fear, without enmity, whose form is beyond time (that is, whose being is imperishable), who does not come into births, whose light is self-existent, and who is found through the True Guru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. Truth Is The Name. Creative Being Personified. No Fear. No Hatred. Image Of The Undying. Beyond Birth. Self-Existent. By Guru's Grace:
There is but one God. True is His Name, Creative His personality and Immortal His form. He is without fear, sans enmity, beyond birth and self-illumined. By the Guru's grace He is obtained.
U2YT: Savaiye uttered by Guru Arjan Dev ji.
Swaiyas From The Mouth Of The Great Fifth Mehl:
Saways recited in person by the sire, 5th Guru.
G15N: Purakh = all-pervading. Karan kaaran = the cause of causes, the root of creation.
O Primal Being! O Creator! You Yourself are the root of all creation.
O Primal Lord God, You Yourself are the Creator, the Cause of all causes.
O my primal Lord, the Creator, You Yourself are the Doer of all the deeds.
O Primal Being, Maker of all beings, (karan kaaran) Creator of the world! Maya, the cause of the great principle and the rest — You Yourself have become all of it.
H8MN: Bharpoor = pervading. Sagal ghat = in all hearts. Rahio biaape = are pervading, are spread out, are ever-present.
You fill every place (that is, there is no place where You are not). You are present in all bodies.
You are All-pervading everywhere, totally filling all hearts.
You are fully filling all and are contained in all hearts.
The whole world is filled within You, and You are pervading all hearts.
D6TM: Dekheeai = are seen. Jagat = in the world. Pat = Master.
O Akal Purakh, Master (of all)! You are seen spread through the whole world. Who knows what You are like? You Yourself protect all (beings).
You are seen pervading the world; who can know Your State? You protect all; You are our Lord and Master.
O God, You are seen pervading the world. Who can know Yours state? You protect all and You Yourself are their Lord.
So You are seen pervading the world. Who can know Your state? That is, no one can know it. O Hari! You are the Husband of all, and You Yourself protect Your servants.
H3VC: Abinaasee = imperishable. Abigat = unmanifest, without bodily form, invisible, not seen with these eyes. Aape aap = from Your own self. Utpat = coming into being.
(O Primal Being!) You are never destroyed; You are not seen with these eyes; Your coming into being is from Your own self alone.
O my Imperishable and Formless Lord, You formed Yourself.
O my Imperishable and Formless Lord, You are born of Yourself.
O imperishable form! You Yourself are the Creator of all; so no one can know Your state.
8MWR: An = any other (anya). Tum bhat = tum bhaant[i], like You.
You are the One and only; there is no other like You.
You are the One and Only; no one else is like You.
You are but One. None else is like You.
You alone are the One and only, for there is no other as mighty as You (bhat) in Your way.
EHVB: Paaraavaar = the near and far shores, the limit. Srab praan ko = of all living beings. Aadhaar = support.
Hari's end and limit (cannot be found). Who is the (person) who can reflect (to find His limit)? Hari is the Father of the whole world and the support of all beings.
O Lord, You have no end or limitation. Who can contemplate You? You are the Father of the world, the Support of all life.
O Lord, You have no end and limit. Who can from Yours conception? You are the Father of the world and the support of all life.

O Hari! So there is no end to Your far and near shores. Who is there who could reflect on Your far and near shores? That is, no one. You are the Father of all the world and the support of the breath of all; meaning, giving Your power, You make the breaths move.
DL5Y: Dar = at the door, at the door (of Akal Purakh). Tul = accepted. Braham samsar = equal to Akal Purakh, the form of Akal Purakh. Jeeh = tongue. Bakhaanai = say, can say.
(Hari's) devotee and servant, (Guru) Nanak, (has been) accepted at (Hari's) door and is like Hari. What (virtues of that Guru Nanak) can (my) one tongue describe?
Your devotees are at Your Door, O God - they are just like You. How can servant Nanak describe them with only one tongue?
O Lord, how can Your slave Nanak, recite with his one tongue the praise of the saint, who is poised at Your door and is like You?

Sri Guru Arjan Dev ji says: O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji! (The word 'Nanak' is to be applied both ways, like a lamp set on the threshold.) I am a devotee at Your door; so I have reflected that You are (tul) like Brahm. What can my one tongue say of Your praise? That is, it cannot say it.
4909: I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, for ever a sacrifice (to Guru Nanak). ||1||
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to them. ||1||
I am a sacrifice, sacrifice, sacrifice, sacrifice and ever a sacrifice to him.
(Haan ki) O True Guru! With the mind I am a sacrifice to You again and again, with the body too I am a sacrifice, and with speech I am for ever a sacrifice. ||1||
DXJD: Amrit = the water of the Name, which gives spiritual life. Pravaah = springs, streams, fountains. Sar = flow, run. Atul = that cannot be weighed. Bhandaar = treasures. Bhar = are full. Apar apaar = boundless.
(O Akal Purakh!) Streams of amrit are flowing (from You); Your treasures, that cannot be weighed, are full; You are beyond the beyond, and boundless.
Streams of Ambrosial Nectar flow; Your Treasures are unweighable and overflowing in abundance. You are the Farthest of the far, Infinite and Incomparably Beautiful.
O Lord, the streams of Nectar flow at your door, brimful are Yours unweighable treasures and You are Infinite, Beauteous, Sublime and the remotest of the remote.

At Your door flow streams of katha and kirtan like amrit, and Your treasures beyond weighing are full; beyond humans are the gods, and beyond them Brahma and the rest; O Boundless One, You are beyond even them, beyond all.
2Z8Z: Bhaavan = will. Kar = You do. Mantr = in counsel. Doosro = anyone else. Na dhar = do not bring in. Opat = creation, the coming into being of the world. Parlau = the destruction of the world. Ekai nimakh = in one instant, in the blink of an eye. Tu = (tav) Your. Ghar = in the house.

You do as You will; You do not bring anyone else into Your counsel (that is, You take no one else's advice). In Your house (that is, by Your Command) the creation and the end of the world happen in the blink of an eye.
You do whatever You please; You do not take advice from anyone else. In Your Home, creation and destruction happen in an instant.
You do what pleases You, take not the counsel of another and in Your Home, creation and destruction occur in am instant.
Whatever pleases You, that You do, and You do not take anyone else's counsel; and the creation and dissolution of the world You bring about in a single instant — (tu ghar) such is Your house.
RRXJ: Aan = any other. Samsar = equal, like. Ujeeaaro = light, radiance. Nirmar = nirmal, clean (Sanskrit 'nirmaalya': pure, clean, stainless; from this the Prakrit and Punjabi forms nirmal, nirmaar, nirmar). Kot paraachhat = millions of sins. Jaahi = are removed.
There is no other like Hari; His light is pure; by taking that Hari's Name, millions of sins are removed.
No one else is equal to You; Your Light is Immaculate and Pure. Millions of sins are washed away, chanting Your Name, Har, Har.
My Lord God, none else is equal to You, immaculate is Your light and reciting Your Name, millions of sins are washed off.
There is none equal to You, and Your (ujeeaaro) light is pure; so, O Hari, by uttering Your Name 'Hari Hari', people's millions of sins are removed.
6F3L: Hari's devotee and servant, (Guru) Nanak, (has been) accepted at (Hari's) door and is like Hari. What (virtues of that Guru Nanak) can (my) one tongue say?
Your devotees are at Your Door, God - they are just like You. How can servant Nanak describe them with only one tongue?
O Lord, how can Your slave Nanak recite with his one tongue, the praise of the saint, who is poised at Your door and is like You?

Sri Guru Arjan Dev ji says: O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji! (The word 'Nanak' is to be applied both ways, like a lamp set on the threshold.) I am a devotee at Your door; so I have reflected that You are (tul) like Brahm. What can my one tongue say of Your praise? That is, it cannot say it.
PLPV: I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, for ever a sacrifice (to Guru Nanak). ||2||
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to them. ||2||
I am a sacrifice, sacrifice, sacrifice, sacrifice, and ever a sacrifice to him.
(Haan ki) O True Guru! With the mind I am a sacrifice to You again and again, with the body too I am a sacrifice, and with speech I am for ever a sacrifice. ||2||
0VQT: Sagal bhavan = all the realms, all the worlds. Dhaare = made, established. Ek then = from the One (His own self). Bisthaare = expanse, spread. Poor rahio = pervades. Niraare = distinct, apart, detached.
That Hari has made all the worlds; from His own one self He made (this) expanse (of the world); He Himself pervades all (and yet) is detached.
You established all the worlds from within Yourself, and extended them outward. You are All-pervading among all, and yet You Yourself remain detached.
You, O Lord, have installed all the world's from within You alone, You have extended them. You are fully contained among them all and yet You Yourself remain detached.

All the (bhavan) worlds are upheld by You — that is, You are the support of all — and from Your one (then) self You have spread out the world's workings. And, O Hari, like space in pot and hall, You alone fill the whole world, and again You shine apart from all. ('Then' is a word of a particular regional dialect.)
ZFQQ: Thaare = Your. Alakh = one who cannot be perceived, whose true form cannot be described. Ko = of. Muraare = O Muraari! The enemy of the demon named Mur (one of the names of Akal Purakh has been used).
O boundless Hari! There is no end or limit to Your virtues; all beings and creatures are Yours; You alone are the Giver of all. Your form cannot be described.
O Lord, there is no end or limit to Your Glorious Virtues; all beings and creatures are Yours. You are the Giver of all, the One Invisible Lord.
O my Unique and Unseeable Lord, the Enemy of ago, You are the giver of all and there is no limit and end to Yours virtues. All the creatures belong to You.
O Hari! There is no end or limit to Your virtues; all these beings, subtle and gross, are (thaare) Yours, and You alone are the Giver of all, the One unseeable Muraari.

B70B: Dhaaran = creation. Dhaare = supports. Dekhaare = shows. Baran = colour. Chihan = mark. Masaare = (Sanskrit shmashru) beard.
(Hari) Himself supports the whole world and shows His creation. He has no colour, no mark, no mouth and no beard.
He Himself supports the Universe, revealing His All-powerful Creative Potency. He has no color, form, mouth or beard.
The Lord Himself upholds the universe and shows His Omnipotence, He has no hue, form, mouth and bread.

You Yourself are the upholder of this (dhaaran) creation, and You show Your (kudrat) Maya; and You have no (baran) colour — or caste such as Brahmin or Kshatriya — no (chihan) marks such as lines, no mouth and no flesh; meaning, You are without attributes.
09JU: Hari's devotee and servant, (Guru) Nanak, (has been) accepted at (Hari's) door and is like Hari. What (virtues of that Guru Nanak) can (my) one tongue say?
Your devotees are at Your Door, O God - they are just like You. How can servant Nanak describe them with only one tongue?
O Lord, how can Your slave Nanak recite with his one tongue the praises of that saint, who is poised at Your door and is like You?

Sri Guru Arjan Dev ji says: O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji! (The word 'Nanak' is to be applied both ways, like a lamp set on the threshold.) I am a devotee at Your door; so I have reflected that You are (tul) like Brahm. What can my one tongue say of Your praise? That is, it cannot say it.
2GAT: I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, for ever a sacrifice (to Guru Nanak). ||3||
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to them. ||3||
I am a sacrifice, yea, a sacrifice, and ever a sacrifice to him.
(Haan ki) O True Guru! With the mind I am a sacrifice to You again and again, with the body too I am a sacrifice, and with speech I am for ever a sacrifice. ||3||
KC3G: Nidhaanan = treasure. Keemat = value. Jaaneejai = is known, is heard. Thaan = abode. Prabh = O Prabhu!
O Prabhu! You are the treasure of all virtues; the value of Your knowledge and of (joining one's) meditation (on You) (cannot be found). Your abode is heard to be the highest of the high.
You are the Treasure of all virtue; who can know the value of Your spiritual wisdom and meditation? O God, Your Place is known as the highest of the high.
My Lord, You are the treasure of all virtues. No one can know the worth of Yours divine wisdom and meditation. The highest of the high is known to be Your seat.
O treasure of all virtues! Your knowledge and meditation have no price; and, O Prabhu, Your place is known to be the highest of all the high.
UD7K: Soot = thread, order, power. Ekai soot = in one order. Upma = comparison, an equal or matching thing. Badaanan = great. Deu = I give.

(O Prabhu!) My mind, my wealth and my breath — all these are (given by) You. The whole world is in Your one power (that is, rests on Your power). Whose name could I give that is equal to You? You are greater than the great.
Mind, wealth and the breath of life belong to You alone, Lord. The world is strung upon Your Thread. What praises can I give to You? You are the Greatest of the great.
My Lord, my soul, riches and vital-breath belong to You. You have strung the world in the one thread of Your system. What praise should I attribute to You? You are the greatest of the great.

Mind, wealth, breath and the whole assembly are Yours alone, and You have strung the world on the one thread of Your power. So, O Prabhu, with whom should I compare You? For You are greater than the great; meaning, only You are like You.
8LGZ: Bhaau [sic: the line reads 'bheu'] = secret, mystery, hidden working. Apaar = boundless. Deu = dev, the Luminous One. Akal kala = the One whose power is without parts, that is, uniform. Dhaanan = support (Sanskrit dhaanan = a receptacle, seat, nourishment).
O Prabhu! Who can know Your secret? O Unseeable One! O Boundless One! O Luminous One! Your power is uniform (everywhere); You are the support of all beings.
Who can know Your Mystery? O Unfathomable, Infinite, Divine Lord, Your Power is unstoppable. O God, You are the Support of all.
O My Incomprehensible and Infinite Luminous Lord, who can know Your secret? Inconceivable is Your power and You are the mainstay of all.

O unseeable, boundless Lord! Who can know Your secret? That is, no one can. For You, my Prabhu, (akal kala) free of all imaginings, sustain all beings by giving (dhaanan) grain; or, it is fitting for all to meditate on You alone.
5638: O Prabhu! (Your) devotee and servant (Guru) Nanak (has been) accepted at (Your) door and (O Prabhu, You) is like Brahm. What (virtues of that Guru Nanak) can (my) one tongue say?
Your devotees are at Your Door, O God - they are just like You. How can servant Nanak describe them with only one tongue?
O Lord, how can Your slave Nanak, with his one tongue, recite the praise of that saint who is poised at Your door and is like You.

Sri Guru Arjan Dev ji says: O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji! (The word 'Nanak' is to be applied both ways, like a lamp set on the threshold.) I am a devotee at Your door; so I have reflected that You are (tul) like Brahm. What can my one tongue say of Your praise? That is, it cannot say it.
UNEK: I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice (to Guru Nanak). ||4||
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to them. ||4||
I ma a sacrifice, yea, a sacrifice, and ever a sacrifice to him.
(Haan ki) O True Guru! With the mind I am a sacrifice to You again and again, with the body too I am a sacrifice, and with speech I am for ever a sacrifice. ||4||
KC48: Nirankaar = without form, beyond colours and marks. Aakaar = with attributes, having form. Achhal = one whom no one can deceive.
You are beyond colours and marks, and You also have form; no one can deceive You; You pervade every place, and You are never destroyed;
O Formless, Formed, Undeceivable, Perfect, Imperishable,
My Lord, You are Formless, Undeceivable, Perfect, and Imperishable,
O Formless One! You Yourself have made form, and, undeceived by Maya, imperishable, You pervade all.
ASB2: Harakhvant = ever joyful. Aanant roop = of endless forms. Bigaasee = blossomed, in full bloom, manifest.
You are ever joyful, Your forms are endless, You are pure in form and plainly manifest.
Blissful, Unlimited, Beautiful, Immaculate, Blossoming Lord:
and Ever in bliss, Ever in bloom, Illimitable, Beauteous, and Immaculate are You.
O pure One, (harakh) full of bliss or zeal, of endless form! Your own power, becoming the world, (bigaasee) blossoms — that is, shines forth.
GE5C: Beant = endless beings. Ik til = even a little. Nahee paasee = is not found.
Endless beings sing Your praises, but not even a little of Your end is found.
Countless are those who sing Your Glorious Praises, but they do not know even a tiny bit of Your extent.
Countless are those who sing Yours praises, however, they know not even a bit of Your limit.
Endless people sing Your praises, but they cannot find even a sesame seed's worth of Your end.
ESSZ: O Prabhu! The person on whom You are merciful meets You.
That humble being upon whom You shower Your Mercy meets with You, O God.
He, to whom You are merciful, O Lord, that person meets with You.
O Prabhu! The person to whom You are merciful — that person merges in Your form.
TJZG: Fortunate are those people on whom Hari has become merciful.
Blessed, blessed, blessed are those humble beings, upon whom the Lord, Har, Har, showers His Mercy.
Blest, blest, and blest are the persons, on whom the Lord God has become merciful.
O Hari! Those people on whom You have been merciful in every way are blessed in all three times.
RUSQ: Har gur Nanak = Guru Nanak, the form of Hari (with such virtues). Jin = those who. Parsiyau = have touched, met, touched the feet of. Si = those (fortunate) people. Duh the = from both. Rahio = are saved. ||5||
Those who have touched Guru Nanak, the form of Hari (with the virtues described above), are saved from both birth and death. ||5||
Whoever meets with the Lord through Guru Nanak is rid of both birth and death. ||5||
Whosoever meets with the Divine Guru Nanak, he is rid of both birth and death.
Sri Guru ji says: O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, form of Hari! Those who have touched — that is, meditated on — Your feet: that company of people has become free of both pains, birth and death. ||5||
H5R9: Sat = everlasting, unchanging. Bhaneeai = is said (that is, people say).
The great souls have always said that Hari is for ever unchanging, ever-abiding;
The Lord is said to be True, True, True, True, the Truest of the True.
True, abidingly true and the truest of the true, my God is said to be.
O Bhagvan! You are called True in form in all four ages and the three times.
1HE8: Avar = other. Aan = any other (anya). Paooraatan = ancient, primal. Suneeai = is heard.
He is heard of as the Primal Being (that is, the root of all); there is no second like Him.
There is no other like Him. He is the Primal Being, the Primal Soul.
He alone is heard to be the primal Lord, There is not another second like him.
O Primal Being! No second like You is heard of in any other place.
9MLS: O mind! Those who have taken Hari's Name, which gives spiritual life, have found every comfort.
Chanting the Ambrosial Name of the Lord, the mortal is blessed with all comforts.
Reciting the ambrosial Name of God, man is blessed with all the comforts.
O Hari! Whoever has taken Your amrit-like Name, the crown of all, has gained every comfort.
VQUS: Jeh = those people who. Rasan = with the tongue. Teh jan = those people (plural). Tripat aghaae = were satisfied. Man = O mind!
Those who have tasted (the Name-amrit) with the tongue are satisfied (that is, they no longer long for other tastes).
Those who taste it with their tongues, those humble beings are satisfied and fulfilled.
They, who taste if with their tongue; those persons are sated and satiated.

Those who have tasted the amrit of Your Name with the tongue — that is, uttered it — (teh) those very people, satisfied with the comforts of this world, are also filled with the comfort of the next; meaning, they are happy in both worlds.
J2K7: Jih = on whom. Tih = their. Bhayo = with the letter 'y' the true vowel sign is (o), but here it is to be read (u). Thaakur = the Master, Prabhu.
Those on whom the Master, Prabhu, has become merciful (have come to) love the company of the holy.
That person who becomes pleasing to his Lord and Master, loves the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation.
He, with whom the Lord becomes pleased, he loves he congregation of the saints.
O Lord of all! Those with whom You are well pleased — they alone have come to love Your true sangat.
HV98: Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, the form of Hari (such as this), have carried their whole lineage across. ||6||
Whoever meets with the Lord through Guru Nanak, saves all his generations. ||6||
Whosoever meets with the God-incarnate Guru Nanak, he emancipates his entire lineage.
O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, form of Hari! Those who have touched Your lotus feet have saved all their lineages. ||6||
9S5T: Sabha = assembly, court. Sach = ever-abiding. Deebaan = court of justice. Sache pahi = with the Guru, the form of the ever-abiding Hari.
(Akal Purakh's) assembly is for ever unchanging, (His) court is ever-abiding; (Akal Purakh has) placed (His own self) with His ever-abiding form, the Guru (that is, Hari is met through the Guru),
True is His Congregation and His Court. The True Lord has established Truth.
True is the Lord's congregation and His court. He has placed His True Name with the True Guru.
O True in form! Your assembly too is True, and Your (deebaan) support too is True.
XBQ1: Sachai takhat = on the true throne. Tapaavas = justice.
(Akal Purakh's) abode is the ever-abiding seat, and He (always) does true justice.
Sitting upon His Throne of Truth, He administers True Justice.
Sitting on the True Throne, He administers true justice.

And You have placed Your true Name with the true Guru; meaning, the teaching of Your Name is gained only through the True Guru. And dwelling on the throne in the true Vaikunth, You have done true (tapaavas) justice.
JB9P: Sach = the True (Akal Purakh), the ever-abiding (Prabhu). Sirjiu = has created. Aabhul = one who does not err. Na bhulau = does not err.
The ever-abiding True (Akal Purakh) has created the world; He Himself is never mistaken, never errs.
The True Lord Himself fashioned the Universe. He is Infallible, and does not make mistakes.
The True Lord, of Himself, has created the world. He is infallible and errs not.

And, O True in form, You Yourself brought the world into being. As it is said: 'He Himself is True, and all that He upholds is true.' And again: 'He Himself is True, and all He made is true.' And You, of unerring form, never err. As it is said: 'All are liable to err; only the Guru, the Creator, does not err.'
UX0P: Keem = value. Nahu = not. Amulau = is priceless.
The excellent Name (of Akal Purakh) (too) is boundless and priceless; the value (of His Name) cannot be found.
The Naam, the Name of the Infinite Lord, is the jewel. Its value cannot be appraised - it is priceless.
Priceless like the jewel is the Name of the Infinite Lord. The worth of the invaluable Name can be prized not.
So, O boundless form! The jewel of Your Name is priceless, for no one can put a price on this Name-jewel.
HFHP: Those on whom Akal Purakh has become merciful — they alone have found every comfort.
That person, upon whom the Lord of the Universe showers His Mercy obtains all comforts.
On whomsoever the world-Lord becomes merciful, he alone obtains all the comfort.
O Gobind! Those people to whom You have been merciful have gained every comfort.
M4TP: Bahurr = again, returning. Jon na aae = did not take birth, were not born. Gabind = with the letter 'g' the true vowel sign is (o); here it is to be read (u). Tinhoo = they alone. ||7||
Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, the form of Akal Purakh (with such virtues), do not come back into birth (and death) again. ||7||
Those who touch the Feet of the Lord through Guru Nanak, do not have to enter the cycle of reincarnation ever again. ||7||
They who touch the feet of Divine Guru Nanak, they are cast not into existences afterwards again.
O Guru Nanak Dev ji, form of Hari! Those who have (parsio) touched — that is, worshipped — Your feet have not come into the womb again; meaning, they have become free of birth and death. ||7||
X76S: Kavan bidh = in what way? by what method?
What yoga (practice) should we do? What knowledge (should we reflect on)? What meditation (should we hold)? What method should we use by which we could sing the praises of Akal Purakh?
What is the Yoga, what is the spiritual wisdom and meditation, and what is the way, to praise the Lord?
What is the 'yoga, ' what the knowledge and contemplation and what the way, by which we can praise our Lord?

O Prabhu! What is that yoga, what is that knowledge, and what is that meditation by which we might be joined to You, know You, and fix the mind's attention on You? And what is that method by which we might utter Your praise?
Q49V: Saadhak = practitioners, people striving for spiritual life. Tetees kor = the thirty-three crore gods. Tir = a sesame seed's worth, even a little. Keem = value. Pareeai = cannot be found.
Even the siddhas, the practitioners and the thirty-three crore gods could not find even a little of Akal Purakh's value.
The Siddhas and seekers and the three hundred thirty million gods cannot find even a tiny bit of the Lord's Value.
The adepts, the strivers and the thirty-three millions of gods, can find not even an iota of the Lord's worth.
The siddhas who hold the eight powers and the rest, and the (saadhak) practitioners, and the thirty-three crore gods — by none of these is even a (tir) sesame seed's worth of Your value found.
2LYR: Brahmaadik = Brahma and the other gods (Brahm-aadik). Sankaad = (Sanak-aad[i]), Sanak and others: Sanak, Sanatan, Sanat-Kumar and Sanandan; these four were the sons of Brahma. Sekh = Shesh Naag; the old Hindu idea is that he has a thousand hoods and is Vishnu's seat; the idea is also current that Shesh Naag holds the whole creation up on his hood.
Brahma and the other gods, Sanak and the rest (Brahma's sons), and Shesh Naag could not find the end of Akal Purakh's virtues.
Neither Brahma, nor Sanak, nor the thousand-headed serpent king can find the limits of His Glorious Virtues.
Neither Brahma, nor Sanak nor the serpent-king, know the limit of His praises.
Brahma ji and the other makers of the world, the ascetics Sanak and the rest, and Shesh Naag — even these do not find the end of Your virtues.
W0X5: Agahu = (a-gahu) beyond grasp, the One whom one cannot reach. Poor = pervading. Gahio = grasped. Srab = all.
(Akal Purakh) is beyond (human) understanding; His state cannot be found; He pervades every place and is present in all.
The Inapprehensible Lord cannot be apprehended. He is pervading and permeating among all.
The Unseizable Lord can be seized not although, He is fully contained among all.
So, O form beyond grasp! You are not grasped by anyone, and You, complete, are (samaai) pervading all beings.
0YEN: Jih = of which people. Silak = noose (of Maya). Prabh = by Prabhu. Sei jan = those people (plural). Bhagte = in devotion.
Those whose noose (of attachment to Maya) the merciful Prabhu has cut have become absorbed in His devotion.
Those whom God has mercifully freed from their nooses - those humble beings are attached to His devotional worship.
They, whose noose the merciful Master has cut off, those persons are attached to His meditation.
O Prabhu! Those on whom You have been merciful and cut the (silak) noose of Maya, desire or attachment — (se) those very people are absorbed in Your devotion.
4W61: It ut = here and there, in this world and the next. Mukte = liberated, free of bonds. ||8||
Those who have touched Guru Nanak, the form of Hari (with such virtues as described above) — those beings are saved from the bonds of Maya in this world and the next. ||8||
Those who meet with the Lord through Guru Nanak are liberated forever, here and hereafter. ||8||
They, who meet with God and Guru Nanak, are ever emancipated here and hereafter.
O Guru Nanak Sahib ji, form of Hari! Those who have touched You have become for ever liberated (it ut) in this world and the next. ||8|| ☬ Now, in the manner of the bards, he begs of Vahiguru ji:
U7DL: Paryiu = has fallen. Jaachak = beggar. Sarna = refuge.
O Prabhu! O Giver! O Bountiful One! I, a beggar, have come to Your refuge;
I am a beggar; I seek the Sanctuary of God, the Giver of givers.
I, the mumper, have sought the refuge of Lord, the Donor of the donors.
O Prabhu, Giver of all gifts! I, one (jaachak) beggar, have fallen at the refuge of Your feet. ☬ If You ask, "What do you beg for?", he says to that:
J1KY: Daan = alms. Sant ren = the dust of the feet of the sangat's members. Jeh lag = by whose support, taking the shelter of which (dust). Bhaujal = the whirlpool (of the world). Tarna = may be crossed.
May (I, the beggar,) receive the alms of the dust of the feet of the sangat's members, so that, taking the shelter of this dust, I may cross the whirlpool (of the world).
Please bless me with the gift of the dust of the feet of the Saints; grasping them, I cross over the terrifying world-ocean.
Bless You me with the bounty of the dust of the saints feet, attached to which I shall cross the dreadful world ocean.
May I be granted the gift of the dust of Your saints' feet, by (lag) meeting which the world-ocean is crossed.
XGPH: O Lord! If it pleases You, (by Your mercy) hear (my) plea; I make one request:
Please listen to my prayer, if it pleases You, O my Lord and Master.
If it pleases You, O Lord, hearken You to my prayer and supplication.
So I make my plea with (binat) supplication — that is, with humility; but, O Lord, if it pleases You, then hear such a request of mine:

YQRA: Man = in (my) mind. Chaau = longing. Bhagat = in (Your) devotion. Ihu man = this mind of mine. Thahraavai = may settle.
Give (me) Your vision; this is the longing in my mind; (have mercy,) may this mind of mine settle in Your devotion.
My mind yearns for the Blessed Vision of Your Darshan. This mind abides in devotional worship.
My mind's yearning is that you may bless me with Your vision, O Lord, this soul of mine abides in Yours meditation.
Give me that vision of Yours for which my mind has (chaau) eagerness, by which my mind may settle — that is, become steady — in Your devotion.
T5ZP: Charaag = lamp. Andhyaar mah = in the darkness. Kal = creation. Udharee = has crossed over. Naam dharam = through the dharma of remembering Hari's Name.
A lamp (Guru Nanak) has been lit in the darkness; by the blessing of the Name (taught by him) the whole creation is crossing over.
The lamp is lit in the darkness; all are saved in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga, through the One Name and faith in the Dharma.
The Name's lamp is kindled in the midst of spiritual darkness. All the men of the Darkage are saved with the aid of the One Name.

To remove the darkness of sins, or of ignorance, that had spread in this Kali age, O Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji, You took birth and lit the lamp of the Name and of knowledge; by that one dharma of chanting the Name, the whole creation of the (kal) Kali age has been saved.
SKZC: Bhavan = world. Har = O Hari! Jan Nanak = (Your) servant (Guru) Nanak. ||9||
Your servant, O Parbrahm, Guru Nanak, Your very form, has become manifest in the whole world. ||9||
The Lord is revealed in all the worlds. O servant Nanak, the Guru is the Supreme Lord God. ||9||
The Guru-God, slave Nanak has become manifest in all the worlds of the Lord.

Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji says: I am Your (jan) servant; O Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, incarnation of Hari, the Parbrahm! You are manifest in all the worlds. ||9|| ☬ To remove the bodily identification of those Bhatts who were the Vedas in form, Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji gives this teaching:
GKL5: Savaiye uttered from the holy mouth of Guru Arjan Dev.
Swaiyas From The Mouth Of The Great Fifth Mehl:
Swayas recited in person by the Sire, 5th Guru.
99DV: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the True Guru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By the True Guru's grace, is He obtained.
HQLF: Kaachee = not lasting. Deh = body. Moh baandhee = bound by attachment (to Maya). Phun = then. Sath = wicked. Kathor = hard-hearted. Kucheel = living in filth. Kugiaanee = foolish, ignorant.
I am wicked, hard-hearted, given to bad deeds and foolish. (First of all, my) body is not lasting; and on top of that it is held tight by attachment,
This body is frail and transitory, and bound to emotional attachment. I am foolish, stone-hearted, filthy and unwise.
Perishable is my body and still it is bound to worldly love. I am foolish, stone-hearted, filthy and unwise.

O brother! Within this unbaked — that is, false — body, this being has further bound its intellect with attachment. Because of this, this (sath) fool, through hardness, has become (kucheel) impure or dirty with the filth of sins, and (kugiaanee) false knowledge has taken hold; meaning, it takes the not-self for the self.
FGCT: Dhaavat bhramat = I wander about. Rahan = steadiness, stability. Nahee paavat = is not found, is not gained. Gat = secret, the high spiritual state.
(Because of this attachment) I wander about; (the mind) does not settle; nor have I known what Parmatma is like.
My mind wanders and wobbles, and will not hold steady. It does not know the state of the Supreme Lord God.
My mind wanders and wabbles and is held not. It knows not the state of Supreme Lord.

Among the things that (dhaavat) pass away — that is, are perishable — it always wanders; or, it runs among thoughts, and so wanders through births. And it has not known the state of Parbrahm; that is why it finds no steadiness.
PL2Y: Joban = youth. Roop = handsome looks. Mad = pride. Maata = intoxicated. Bicharat = I wander. Bikal = distraught, forgetting oneself.
I am intoxicated with the pride of youth, handsome looks and Maya; forgetting myself, I wander about, and I am very proud.
I am intoxicated with the wine of youth, beauty and the riches of Maya. I wander around perplexed, in excessive egotistical pride.
I am intoxicated with the wine of youth, beauty and riches and wander about perplexed in great ego.
Intoxicated with the pride of Maya through youth and handsome form, the very (abhimaanee) proud being, distraught with pains, wanders through births.
NJ4J: Apvaad = bad words, bitter speech. Naar = (another's) woman (looking with an evil eye). Yah = these. Jeea maah = in the heart. Hitaanee = seem dear.
Another's wealth, backbiting against others, looking at another's woman with an evil eye, and slandering others — these things seem sweet and dear to me in my heart.
The wealth and women of others, arguments and slander, are sweet and dear to my soul.
Another's wealth and another's wranglings, women and slander, these are sweet and dear to my mind.

Another's wealth, and (par apbaad) idle talk about others and speaking behind their backs — this slander of others — and love for another's woman: this whole array of vices this being has taken for sweet and brought into its heart with fondness; meaning, it is full of these vices.
UN33: Balbanch upaava = schemes of deceit. Chhap = in secret. Karat = I do. Pekhat = You see. Sunat = (You) hear. Prabh = O Prabhu!
O inner-knowing Prabhu! I make schemes of deceit in secret, (but) You see and hear.
I try to hide my deception, but God, the Inner-knower, the Searcher of Hearts, sees and hears all.
I make efforts to conceal my frauds, however, my Master, the Inner knower, sees and hears all.

By force, by (banch) cheating, by hiding — that is, by theft — it makes many such schemes for the sake of wealth; but that inner-knowing Prabhu sees and hears this being's deeds; meaning, He knows everything. So, giving up these vices, let the being make a request to that Vahiguru like this:
VW5L: Seel = good nature. Such = purity. Naast = is not (na-asti). Aaio = I have come. Jeea ke daanee = O Giver of the soul! O Giver of the gift of life!
O Giver of the gift of life! I have neither good nature nor dharma, neither compassion nor purity. I have come to Your refuge.
I have no humility, faith, compassion or purity, but I seek Your Sanctuary, O Giver of life.
I have no humility, faith, compassion or piety, however, I have sought Your refuge, O the Giver of spiritual life.
O Vahiguru! In me there is (naast) no virtue — no (seel) calm, no dharma, compassion or (such) purity; but, knowing You as the Giver of the gift of life, I have come to Your refuge.
XGDX: Kaaran karan = O root of creation! Sireedhar = O Master of Maya! ||1||
O almighty Creator of creation! O Master of Maya! O Lord of Nanak! Save (me from these). ||1||
The All-powerful Lord is the Cause of causes. O Lord and Master of Nanak, please save me! ||1||
God, the Lord of wealth, is Omnipotent to do everything, O the Master of Nanak, now save You him in Your mercy.

O You who are able to make the (kaaran) great principle and the rest! O (sireedhar) holder of Lakshmi, Lord of Your servants! By Your grace save me from the world-ocean. Sri Guru ji says: by making such a request, one is set free. ||1||
EMQ5: Man mohan = of Hari who enchants the mind. Keerat karan = singing praise. Saran = taking refuge. Johan = jodhan, warriors. Bidaaran kau = to destroy, to remove.
Praising Hari who enchants the mind, and taking His refuge — these are able to destroy (beings') sins (that is, if we take Hari's refuge and sing His praise, sins are removed).
The Praises of the Creator, the Enticer of the mind, are potent to destroy sins.
To praise God, the soul-charmer and to seek His refuge, these are potent to dispel and destroy one's sins.

Uttering the praise of Vahiguru, and coming to the refuge of that Enchanter of the mind — these two deeds are able to destroy sins. Or: these two deeds (johan) look to the destruction of sins; meaning, by doing them all sins are removed.
1J00: Taaran taran = the boat to carry across (the world-ocean). Taran = boat. Sabhai bidh = in every way, fully. Kulah samooh = hosts of lineages, many lineages. Udhaaran sau = to save, to carry across.
Hari is the ship to carry (beings across the world-ocean), and is fully able to carry across the many lineages (of the devotees).
The All-powerful Lord is the boat, to carry us across; He saves all our generations.
In every way All-powerful God is a ship for crossing the world ocean and He can emancipate the entire lineage of His slave.
Hari, like a (taran) ship for carrying across, is able in every way, and He saves the whole host of (sau) hundreds of the lineages of His devotees.
7T2Z: Chit achet = O heedless mind! Chet = remember. Jaan = recognise. Bharam andher mohio = robbed by the darkness of doubt. Kat = where? Dhaun = you run about, you wander.
O (my) heedless mind! Remember (Ram), form a bond with the company of the holy; robbed by the darkness of doubt, where are you wandering?
O my unconscious mind, contemplate and remember Him in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation. Why are you wandering around, enticed by the darkness of doubt?
O my headless soul, realise that the Lord in the saints' society, and contemplate on Him. Why wander you beguiled by the darkness of doubt?

So, O heedless mind! To know His form, (chet) remember the Name through the company of the saints; for without remembering the Name, enchanted by the darkness of doubt, where do you go (dhaun) running about?
SJDC: Moorat = a muhurat. Gharee = ghari. Simran = (do) remembrance. Rasna sang = with the tongue. Lau = take.
Even for a muhurat, a ghari, a chasa or a pal, remember Ram; remember Ram's Name with the tongue.
Remember Him in meditation, for an hour, for a moment, even for an instant. Chant the Name of the Lord with your tongue.
Meditate you on God, even for a moment, half a moment, an instant and trice and, with your tongue, recite you the Lord's Name.
So for a muhurat of two gharis, or one ghari, or a pal and a (chasa) — that is, at every moment — remembering with the mind, (lau) utter Ram's Name with the tongue.
2QK3: Hochhau = shallow, not lasting to the end. Kaaj = work, business. Alap = little. Bandhan = the means of trapping. Kot = millions. Kaha = why? for whose sake? (in pains). Bhaun = you will wander.
(This worldly) business does not last for ever; these little comforts (of Maya) are the cause of trapping (the being); (for their sake) why will (you) wander in pains through millions of births?
You are bound to worthless deeds and shallow pleasures; why do you spend millions of lifetimes wandering in such pain?
Bound with the worthless deeds and momentary pleasures, why wander you among pain in millions of births?
For the little pleasures of the senses, which are bonds, you get caught in (hochhau) trifling affairs and (bhau) wander through millions upon millions of births; why do you take on pains?
FGZ9: Sikhya = teaching (taking). Nanak = O Nanak! Rang = in the colour. Aatam siu = with your own soul. Raun = enjoy. ||2||
So, O Nanak, taking the teaching of the saints, remember the Name, and (absorbed) in Ram's colour, find bliss within yourself. ||2||
Chant and vibrate the Name of the Lord, O Nanak, through the Teachings of the Saints. Meditate on the Lord with love in your soul. ||2||
O Nanak, by the saint's instruction, you recite the Name and with hearty love, meditate on your Lord.

Sri Guru ji says: O brother! Taking the teaching of the saints, chant only Vahiguru's Name, and with the (rang) love of the (aatam) mind, delight in that all-pervading Ram. ||2|| ☬ What is that Ram like?
9Q7R: Ranchak ret = a little seed. Khet = field. Tan = in the body (that is, in the mother's womb). Khet tan = in the field of the mother's womb. Nirmit = sown. Deh = body. Durlabh = priceless. Savaar = adorning.
(O being! Parmatma) sowed a little (of the father's) seed in the field of the mother's womb and set up (your) priceless (human) body, adorned.
The little sperm is planted in the body-field of the mother, and the human body, so difficult to obtain, is formed.
Sowing a little sperm in the field of the mother's body, the Lord has created the priceless human body.
That Vahiguru who, by bringing a mere trace of the father's (ret) seed into the field of the mother's womb, (savaar) formed this very rare human body.
EP6W: Khaan paan = things to eat and drink. Sodhe = mansions. Sukh bhunchat = comforts to enjoy (given). Sankat = suffering (that is, the suffering of lying upside down in the mother's womb). Kaat = cutting, removing. Bipat = trouble, hardship. Haree = removed.
(He gave you) things to eat and drink, mansions and comforts to enjoy; cutting away suffering, He removed your trouble.
He eats and drinks, and enjoys pleasures; his pains are taken away, and his suffering is gone.
To enable him to enjoy pleasures, the Lord blesses man with articles of food and drink and mansions and wards off his pain and rids him of his calamity.
By whose grace this being enjoys the comforts of food, drink and (sodhe) mansions; and Vahiguru, the cutter of suffering, removed this being's painful trouble of staying in the womb.
G7DT: Ar = and. Bandhap = relatives, kin. Boojhan kee = of recognising. Soojh = understanding, intellect. Paree = (came into your mind).
(O being! By Parmatma's grace) then the understanding to recognise mother, father, brother and kin came into you.
He is given the understanding to recognize mother, father, siblings and relatives.
The entire understanding to recognise his mother, father, brothers and the Kinsmen, man has obtained from the Lord.
By whose grace it gained the understanding to (boojhan) recognise mother, father, brother and all relatives.
KQZN: Bardhamaan hovat = grows. Din prat = every day, day by day. Nit = always. Nikat = near. Bikhamm = fearsome. Jaree = old age.
Day by day (your body) keeps growing, and fearsome old age is drawing near.
He grows day by day, as the horrible specter of old age comes closer and closer.
Day by day, the mortal is ever growing and the dreadful old age is drawing close to him.
This body, by the grace of that Ram, (bardhamaan) grows day by day — that is, keeps increasing. So, O brother, now (jaree) old age, which is very (bikham) hard, keeps coming near you.
2TTT: Gunheen = empty of virtues. Deen = pauper. Krim = worm.
O you empty of virtues, pauper, worm of Maya! Remember for (at least) one ghari that Master (who has given you so many gifts).
You worthless, petty worm of Maya - remember your Lord and Master, at least for an instant!
O despicable and virtueless worm of wealth, contemplate on your Lord even for a moment.

O you empty of virtues! O worm of Maya, made a pauper for the sake of sense-objects! O being! Remember for at least one ghari that Master who has given you everything. ☬ If you ask what that remembrance is like, he says: make a request before Him like this:
VZN7: Kar = hand. Gah = taking. Gah lehu = take hold. Kripaal = O merciful Hari. Kripaanidh = O treasure of mercy! Kaat = remove. Bharamm bharee = the bundle of doubts. ||3||
O Merciful One! O ocean of mercy! Take hold of Nanak's hand and take off the bundle of doubts. ||3||
Please take Nanak's hand, O Merciful Ocean of Mercy, and take away this heavy load of doubt. ||3||
O the Ocean of compassion, my Merciful Master, You hold Nanak's hand and rid him of his load of doubt.
O most merciful treasure of mercy! Take hold of my hand. And Sri Guru ji says: my intellect is full of doubt; cut away that doubt. ||3||
CELM: Moos = mouse. Bila = burrow. Garbat = (you) are proud. Kartab = deeds, doings. Mahaan mughnaan = of the great fools.
O mind! (You are proud in this body just as) a mouse is proud living in its burrow, and you do the deeds of great fools.
O mind, you are a mouse, living in the mousehole of the body; you are so proud of yourself, but you act like an absolute fool.
O my mind's mouse, living in your body hole, you pride on yourself and does the deeds of a great fool.
O mind, you (moos) mouse! Sitting in the (bila) burrow of the body you are proud, and you do the deeds of great fools.
D0SK: Sampat = wealth, things. Dol = swing, cradle. Jhol = swaying. Jhol sang = with the swaying. Jhoolat = (you) swing. Magan = intoxicated. Ghughna = like an owl.
(You) are swinging high in the cradle of Maya, and, intoxicated with Maya, you wander about like an owl.
You swing in the swing of wealth, intoxicated with Maya, and you wander around like an owl.
You sway with the swing of the cradle of riches and intoxicated with wealth, wander like an owl.
You swing with the (jhol) swaying of the (dol) litter or cradle of wealth; and so, become like an (ghughna) owl, you wander absorbed in Maya.
Z7XN: Sut = son. Banita = wife. Ta siu = with these. Badhio = has grown. Ghana = much.
Son, wife, friends, (worldly) comforts and relatives — (your) attachment to these is growing very great.
You take pleasure in your children, spouse, friends and relatives; your emotional attachment to them is increasing.
For your own pleasure, you are involved with yours sons, wife, friends and kinsmen and your love for them immensely increases each day.
So (sut) son, (banita) wife, the comforts of dearest friends, and (bandhap) brothers and other such relatives — your attachment to them has grown exceedingly (ghana) great.
MAY2: Aham = ego. Mam = possessiveness. Ankur = sprout. Audh = lifespan. Aghnaan = sins.
You have sown the seed of ego (within yourself), (from which) the sprout of possessiveness (is growing); your life is passing in committing sins.
You have planted the seeds of egotism, and the sprout of possessiveness has come up. You pass your life making sinful mistakes.
You have sown the seed of ego, and from it sprouted the plumule of mineness and your life passes committing sins.
You have sown the seed of ego in your heart; from it the sprout of possessiveness has come up; so your lifespan passes in committing (aghna) sins.
2V0V: Mirat = death. Manjaar = tomcat. Mukh pasaar = opening the mouth. Nirkhat = watches. Bhunchat bhugat = enjoying pleasures again and again. Bhugat = the pleasures of the world. Bhookh = craving.
The cat of death is watching (you) with its mouth open, (but) you are enjoying pleasures. Even so, under craving, (you) remain hungry.
The cat of death, with his mouth wide-open, is watching you. You eat food, but you are still hungry.
The cat of death is watching you with his mouth wide-opened. Even while taking food, you are hungry due to desires (for more).

The one who (bhunchat) eats the food of beings and still stays hungry with the craving to eat them — that is, who is never satisfied however many beings it kills — that cat of death, its mouth open, is watching you in order to eat you. Or: O being! The cat of death, its mouth open, is watching you, and you, enjoying those things, stay hungry with the hunger of craving at all three times; meaning, you want to enjoy them still more.
JB28: O (mind of) Nanak! Knowing the world to be a dream, remember the merciful Gopal, Hari, (staying) in the company of the holy. ||4||
Meditate in remembrance on the Merciful Lord of the World, O Nanak, in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation. Know that the world is just a dream. ||4||
Says Nanak, in the saints' society, remember you the Merciful Master, the Cherisher of the universe and deem the world to be just a dream.
Sri Guru ji says: O brother! Keeping the company of the most merciful saints, who know the world to be unreal like a dream, remember Gopal. ||4||

UWXJ: Deh = body. Geh = house. Neh = attachment, love. Na neeta = impermanent, not lasting for ever. Mat = intoxicated, proud. Kaha lau = until when? Gaarahu = (you) will be proud.
O (being) intoxicated with Maya! This body, this house, these loves (of Maya) — none of them lasts for ever; until when will (you) be proud (of them)?
Neither body, nor house, nor love last forever. You are intoxicated with Maya; how long will you be proud of them?
Neither body, nor house, nor love; these last not for ever. Intoxicated with riches, how ling shall you take pride on them?

O being! Attachment to this body and (geh) house and such things is not eternal; that is, it is unreal. Intoxicated with Maya, how long will you be (gaarahu) proud in them — or, how long will you wear yourself away in them?
KFVT: Chhatr = royal canopy. Patr = written order, decree. Chaavar = those who wave the whisk. Bahtee jaat = is passing away (that is, they will perish). Ridai = in the heart.
These (royal) canopies, these decrees, these whisks and these whisk-bearers will all perish. But you do not reflect on this in your heart.
Neither crown, nor canopy, nor servants last forever. You do not consider in your heart that your life is passing away.
Neither throne and crown, nor royal warrants, nor fly-brushes and their waveres shall stay. You remember not that your life is passing off.

For in the next world neither the canopy will go, nor the (patr) decree — that is, no order will run — nor the whisk, nor the (chaavar) whisk-bearer; nor will there be any (chaavar) rice. So the river of your lifespan keeps flowing — that is, passing — but you do not reflect on this in your heart.
7UVU: Asv = horses. Gaj = elephants. Singhaasan = throne. Chhin mah = very quickly. Tiaagat = leaving. Naang = naked. Sidhaarahu = you will depart.
Chariots, horses, elephants, thrones — none (of these will go with you); leaving them in an instant, you will depart naked (from here).
Neither chariots, nor horses, nor elephants or royal thrones shall last forever. In an instant, you will have to leave them, and depart naked.
Neither chariots nor horses, elephants and royal throne shall remain stable. Leaving them off, in a moment, you shall go completely naked.
Neither chariots nor (asv) horses nor (gaj) elephants nor any such mount will go with you; and leaving the throne and all such splendour in a single instant, you will go on bare feet.
HPS5: Soor = heroes. Beer = warriors. Meer = kings. Khaanam = khans, chiefs. Sang = companion. Drist = with the eyes. Nihaarahu = see.
See with your eyes! Neither heroes, nor warriors, nor kings, nor chiefs — none (will be your) companion.
Neither warrior, nor hero, nor king or ruler last forever; see this with your eyes.
Neither warrior, nor hero, nor king and duke; none of these is seen with the eyes going along with you.

Neither heroes, nor (beer) brothers or champions, nor any (meer) nobles, ministers, counsellors and the like, nor (khaanam) Pathans — that is, all those you think of as your helpers — if you look with the eye of reflection, none will go with you there in the next world.
BR3E: Kot = forts. Ot = shelters. Kos = treasuries. Chhota = release. Bikaar = sins. Dooo = both. Kar = hands (plural). Jhaarahu = (you) shake off.
With these forts, (Maya's) shelters and treasuries there will be no release (at the end). (You) commit sin after sin and shake off both hands (that is, sin carelessly).
Neither fortress, nor shelter, nor treasure will save you; doing evil deeds, you shall depart empty-handed.
Neither fortress, nor treasures can emancipate you. Committing sins, you shall depart wiping off both yours hands.

For there, neither by the (ot) shelter of forts nor by the shelter of (kos) treasuries will your (chhota) release come. Committing vices, shaking off both hands — that is, empty-handed — you will go away.
J7G3: Kalatr = wife. Sakh = comrades, companions. Ulatat jaat = turn away, turn back, turn their faces, leave. Chhaarahu = like the shade.
These friends, sons, wife, kin and comrades will leave you (at the end), as the shade of a tree (leaves it in the dark).
Friends, children, spouses and friends - none of them last forever; they change like the shade of a tree.
The intimate, sons, wife, friends and mates stand not by you. They change like the shade of the tree.

Friends, sons, (kalatr) wife, kin, comrades — none will help, for all these things keep turning away like the shade of a tree and like the water of a stream; that is, they keep changing and do not stay the same.
AZ7R: Deen dayaal = merciful to the lowly. Pooran purakh = Hari who pervades every place. Chhin chhin = always, at every moment. Agam = unfathomable, the One whom it is very hard to reach.
(O mind!) Remember at every moment Hari, merciful to the lowly, pervading every place, boundless and beyond limit, (and say):
God is the Perfect Primal Being, Merciful to the meek; each and every instant, meditate in remembrance on Him, the Inaccessible and Infinite.
The Omnipotent and Omnipresent Lord is merciful to the meek. Every moment dwell you upon your Inaccessible and Infinite God.
So, O brother, always, every instant, remember the Lord, merciful to the lowly, unreachable by mind and speech, the boundless, complete Being.
1904: Sreepat = Master of Maya. Sree = Maya. ||5||
"O Master of Maya! O Lord! O Bhagvant! By Your grace carry across Your servant Nanak, who has come to Your refuge." ||5||
O Great Lord and Master, servant Nanak seeks Your Sanctuary; please shower him with Your Mercy, and carry him across. ||5||
O my Illustrious God, the Lord of Lakhshmi and the Master of all, slave Nanak has sought Your refuge. Showering Yours benediction, now save You him.
Sri Guru ji says: O Husband of Lakshmi, Lord of all! O Bhagvant! I am in Your refuge; so by Your grace carry me, Your servant, across this world-ocean. ||5|| ☬ He shows the power of Maya:
U6NJ: Maan = honour. Daan = alms (taking them again and again). Mag johan = watching the road, robbing on the highway again and again. Heet = love. Heet de = forming attachment. Cheet de = paying attention again and again. Paaree = gathered.

(People) risking their lives, giving up even their honour, taking alms again and again, robbing on the highway again and again, forming love (for Maya), giving (full) attention, take and take (Maya) and gather it;
I have used up my breath of life, sold my self-respect, begged for charity, committed highway robbery, and dedicated my consciousness to the love and pursuit of acquiring wealth.
Risking his life, selling his self-respect, receiving alms, committing highway robberies and embracing hearty love, the mortal amasses riches.

(Maya) which watches the (mag) road of those who practise breath-control and of the proud; or, (Maya) which (johan) destroys the road of good deeds such as breath, (maan) respect and charity — O being! Seeing the love of the mind, you have taken it from wherever you could and (paaree) reared it; meaning, gathered it and kept it.
CEF2: Taahoo te = from them. Niraaree = apart, hidden, out of sight.
They keep it hidden out of sight from kin, companions, friends, sons and brothers — from all of them.
I have kept it secretly hidden from my friends, relatives, companions, children and siblings.
The friends, kinsmen, intimates sons and brothers, from them he keeps it concealed.
You have kept it apart even from kin, (sain) companions, friends, sons, brothers and all well-wishers; meaning, you have told no one its secret.
EJQ8: Dhaavan paavan = running about. Koor kamaavan = doing false deeds. Ih bidh = in this way. Audh tan = the lifespan of the body. Jaaree = burned up, wasted.
Running about (after Maya), doing deeds of deceit — (people) waste their whole life doing just this;
I ran around practicing falsehood, burning up my body and growing old.
To obtain it, he runs about and practises falsehood, this wise, he becomes aged.
To get it, running through lands at home and abroad, you have earned only falsehood. Doing things this way, you have spent — that is, passed — the lifespan of the body.
AHPA: Chanchal = Maya, who leaves one's side. Sagal bidh = all deeds, dharma and the rest. Haaree = lost.
Good deeds, living with discipline, spiritual purity and observances — all these they give up in the company of fickle Maya.
I gave up good deeds, righteousness and Dharma, self-discipline, purity, religious vows and all good ways; I associated with the fickle Maya.
In the associating of mercurial mammon, he abandons virtuous deeds, self-control, piety, religious vows and all other good ways.

In the company of this fickle Maya, this being has lost entirely all good deeds and dharma, fasts and self-discipline, purity and the way of observances; meaning, it has become empty of good deeds and dharma.
AMXY: Pankhee = birds. Asthaavar = (sthaavar) mountains and the like, which do not move from their place. Bahu bidh = of many kinds. Bhramio at bhaaree = wandered a great deal.
(Beings) wander a great deal through these many kinds of births — animals, birds, trees, mountains and the like;
Beasts and birds, trees and mountains - in so many ways, I wandered lost in reincarnation.
The animals, birds, trees and mountains; he very greatly wanders in such like existences a various ways.
So, wandering in many ways through all births — animals, birds, trees and other immovable and moving beings, that is, inert and conscious — it suffers very heavy pains.
FS0E: Not even for an instant, a moment or a chasa do they chant the Name of the Lord of the lowly, the Master of breath, the Maker of creation.
I did not remember the Naam, the Name of the Lord, for a moment, or even an instant. He is the Master of the meek, the Lord of all life.
Even for an instant, a trice and a moment, he remembers not the Name of God, the Master of the meek and the Lord of like of the whole world.
Vahiguru, the Lord of the lowly, the Master of the breath of all creation — this being has not remembered His Name even for an instant, a moment or a chasa.
H83E: Khaan paan = eating and drinking. Ant kee baar = at the final hour. Kat = wholly, completely. Khaaree = bitter.
Eating and drinking, things of sweet taste — (all these) always (seem) bitter at the final hour.
The food and drink, and the sweet and tasty dishes became totally bitter at the last moment.
However, the articles of food and drink and the sweet savoury dishes become altogether bitter at the last moment.
So the sweet tastes of food and drink — (kat) how do they help at the end? That is, they do not. In the end they turn bitter; meaning, from enjoying them only pain is gained.
ZYKM: Udhare = went away [sic: printed 'tur gae'; likely 'tar gae', crossed over]. Hor = other people. Magan = sunk, intoxicated. Daaree = daar[i], leaving behind. ||6||
O Nanak! Those who fall at the feet of the saints are carried across; the other people, intoxicated with Maya, leave everything and go (empty-handed). ||6||
O Nanak, I was saved in the Society of the Saints, at their feet; the others, intoxicated with Maya, have gone, leaving everything behind. ||6||
Nanak, One is saved in the society of the saint's feet. Others who are intoxicated with wealth have to quit leaving behind everything.
Sri Guru ji says: those people who are attached to the saints' feet have crossed the world-ocean; and all the ignorant beings absorbed in Maya have left Maya in this very place and gone. ||6||
H43P: Chhand = (chhandas = the Vedas) Vedas. Muneesur = great sages. Rasak = relishing, with love. Thaakur gun = the Lord's virtues.
Those like Brahma, Shiv ji and the great sages sing Parmatma's praises with love through the Vedas.
Brahma, Shiva, the Vedas and the silent sages sing the Glorious Praises of their Lord and Master with love and delight.
Brahma and his likes, Shiva, the Vedas and the silent sages sing the Lord's praises with relish and love.
Starting from Brahma ji, Shiv ji and the (chhand) Vedas, and all the great sages — all of them, (rasak) lovers of that Name, become (rasak) one with it and sing that Lord's praises.
P3UL: Munindr = great sages. Dharan = earth. Gagan = sky. Phun = again. Dhaavat = run.
Indra, the great sages and Gorakh (and others) now come to earth, now run towards the sky, searching (for Parmatma everywhere).
Indra, Vishnu and Gorakh, who come to earth and then go to heaven again, seek the Lord.
Indra, Vishnu and Gorakh, who sometimes land on earth and sometimes go to heaven, search and seek their Lord.

Indra and the other gods, and the king of sages, Gorakh, and the other siddhas who come and go running over earth and sky — that is, those full of power — they too search for that Lord through chanting, austerity and other practices.
KPLC: Sidh = yogis perfected in yogic practices. Dev = gods. Ar = and. Daanav = demons. Ik til = even a sesame seed's worth, even a little. Maram = secret.
Siddhas, humans, gods and demons — none has found even a little of the secret of that (Prabhu).
The Siddhas, human beings, gods and demons cannot find even a tiny bit of His Mystery.
The perfect persons, men, Gods and demons can find not even an iota of His mystery.
In the same way siddhas, humans, gods and demons — none of these can find even a sesame seed's worth of His (maram) secret.
W4RV: Pria prabh = of the beloved Prabhu. Ta kai daras = in His (Prabhu's) vision. Samaavat = merge. Jan = servants.
But Hari's servants, through love of the beloved Prabhu and through devotion full of the taste of love, merge in His vision.
The Lord's humble servants are imbued with love and affection for God their Beloved; in the delight of devotional worship, they are absorbed in the Blessed Vision of His Darshan.
God's slave, who is imbued with the love and affection of his lovable Lord and the relish of His meditation, merges in His vision.
Hari's saints, who are absorbed in the taste of loving devotion through love of that beloved Prabhu, merge in the vision of that Vahiguru; meaning, they become one with His form.
DJV7: Tisahi = Him (Prabhu). Tiaag = leaving. Aan kau = from others. Jaachahi = (those people who) beg. Dant = teeth. Rasan = tongue.
(Those people who) leave that Prabhu and beg from others — (from begging and begging, their) mouth, teeth and tongue all wear away.
But those who forsake Him, and beg from another, shall see their mouths, teeth and tongues wear away.
Abandoning Him, he who asks from another's his mouth, teeth and tongue all wear off.

Those who leave Him and beg from other goddesses and gods — their mouth, teeth, tongue and every limb wear away with begging; meaning, through craving they stay ever lowly, and the openings of their senses grow weak.
M8SE: Moorr = O fool! Sukhdaata = giver of comforts. ||7||
O foolish mind! Remember (Prabhu), the giver of comforts; (Prabhu's) servant Nanak is counselling you. ||7||
O my foolish mind, meditate in remembrance on the Lord, the Giver of peace. Slave Nanak imparts these teachings. ||7||
O my silly soul, you contemplate on the Peace-Giving Lord. Slave Nanak instructs you this wise.
O person of foolish mind! Remember Vahiguru, who is the giver of comforts. Sri Guru ji says: I, the servant of Parmeshvar, am counselling you.
RN7J: Bhram moh kai = because of delusion and attachment. Koop = in the well. Gubaar koop = in the dark well. Pario hai = you have fallen.
The Maya into whose dark well you have fallen through delusion and attachment plays games of many colours.
The pleasures of Maya shall fade away. In doubt, the mortal falls into the deep dark pit of emotional attachment.
The pleasure of worldly valuables fades off. Through doubt, the mortal falls into dark well of worldly love.
The being, through delusion, has fallen into the (gubaar) dark well of attachment through the (rang) love of that Maya which turns one away from Parmeshvar.
CUGV: Gab = pride, ego. Akaas = up to the sky. Na maavat = does not fit. Ast = bones. Krim = worms. Udar = belly.
(You) have so much pride that (you) do not fit even up to the sky. (But all that you are is this:) your belly is full of excrement, bones and worms.
He is so proud, even the sky cannot contain him. His belly is filled with manure, bones and worms.
He prides so such, that he can be contained not even in the sky. His belly is filled with ordure, bones and worms.

So it is this (gab) — in the Naga language this means pride — that is, it is so proud that it does not fit even in the sky; meaning, it thinks itself greater than all and holds even Indra and the rest as trifling. And this being's belly is full of excrement, (ast) bones and worms.
ZF6F: Dahdis = in the ten directions. Dhaai = running and running. Maha bikhia kau = for the sake of very poisonous Maya. Chheen = snatching. Agiaan = foolishness. Hario = robbed.
You run in the ten directions for the sake of Maya, snatch others' wealth; ignorance has robbed you.
He runs around in the ten directions, for the sake of the great poison of corruption. He steals the wealth of others, and in the end, he is destroyed by his own ignorance.
For the sake of great poison, he runs in ten directions, snatches others wealth and is ultimately destroyed by ignorance.
Running in all ten directions for the great pleasures of the senses, it snatches others' wealth; and so its ignorance has robbed it of knowledge.
NW3X: Jara = old age. Rog = the disease. Mirat = death.
(Your) youth has passed; the disease of old age has seized (you); (you) have died such a death (where) you must pay the penalty of Yama's messengers.
His youth passes away, the illnesses of old age seize him, and the Messenger of Death punishes him; such is the death he dies.
His youth passes away, the ailment of old age seizes him, the death's myrimdon punishes him and he dies an ignoble death.
In these vices youth passed; and when the disease of (jara) old age seized it — that is, old age came — then at the time of death Yama's messengers struck this being on the head with their rod.
JZ8V: Sankat = suffering, pain. Bhunchat = you endure. Saasan = (Yama's) rebuke. Dookh garat = in the pit of pains. Gario hai = you are rotting.
You endure the sufferings of countless births and the hells; you are rotting in the pit of the pains of Yama's rebuke.
He suffers the agony of hell in countless incarnations; he rots away in the pit of pain and condemnation.
He suffers agony in the hell of many existences and putrefies in the pit of the pain of censure of the death's minister.
In countless births it endures the (sankat) torments of the hells, and, suffering the pains of the (saasan) rebuke of Yama's messengers, it lies rotting in the pit of the womb.
PC0R: Udharahi = cross over, are carried across. Se = those people. ||8||
O Nanak! Those people whom (Hari) has by His grace Himself made saints have crossed over through the blessing of loving devotion. ||8||
O Nanak, those whom the Saint mercifully takes as his own, are carried across by their loving devotional worship. ||8||
O Nanak, they alone, whom the saint mercifully makes his own, ferry across through the Lord's loving worship.

Sri Guru ji says: those whom the saints by their grace have made into their own form — those people, through loving devotion, come out of this (garat) pit; meaning, they become free of birth and death. ||8||
PMDF: Gun samooh = all virtues. Phal sagal manorath = the fruits of all desires.
(By remembering Hari's Name) our hope has been fulfilled; all virtues and the fruits of all desires have been gained.
All virtues are obtained, all fruits and rewards, and the desires of the mind; my hopes have been totally fulfilled.
I am blessed with all virtues, all boons and my mind's desires and hopes too have been fulfilled.
The host of virtues, the four fruits — dharma, wealth, desire and liberation — and every desire have been gained; and by chanting that Name all our hopes have been fulfilled.
869E: Aukhadh = medicine, herb. Par dukh har = removing others' pains. Khandan = destroying. Gunkaaree = producing virtues.
To remove others' pains (this Name) is a medicine, is a mantra; the Name destroys all diseases and produces virtues.
The Medicine, the Mantra, the Magic Charm, will cure all illnesses and totally take away all pain.
The medicine and spell of the Lord's Name is efficacious to eradicate all ailments and it wholly removes the pain.
And that Name of Hari is a medicine for destroying all diseases, and (par) especially able to take away pains; and it is beneficial like the highest mantra and tantra.

K3WL: Mad = pride. Matsar = envy. Binas jaahi = are destroyed. Uchaaree = by remembering, by uttering.
By remembering Hari's Name, lust, anger, pride, envy and craving — all these are destroyed.
Lust, anger, egotism, jealousy and desire are eliminated by chanting the Name of the Lord.
Reciting the Lord's Name, lust, wrath, ego, jealousy and craving are eradicated.
Lust and anger, (mad) pride, (matsar) envy, craving and every vice are destroyed by uttering the Name of that Hari.
ERRV: Taapan = practising austerities. Such kiria = practices for keeping bodily purity. Charan kamal = Hari's beautiful lotus-like feet.
Bathing (at pilgrimage places), giving charity (there), practising austerities and rites of bodily purity — (in place of all these) we have enshrined Prabhu's feet in the heart.
The merits of cleansing baths, charity, penance, purity and good deeds, are obtained by enshrining the Lotus Feet of God within the heart.
The enshrining of the Lord's lotus feet in the mind bestows the merit of ablution, charity, penance, piety and good actions.

Bathing and charity, (taapan) doing austerities, (kiria) worship and other good deeds done with (such) purity — the root of these is just this: holding love for the lotus feet of that Prabhu in the heart.
3LFH: Jeea dhaan = the support of life, the source of the soul. Praan adhaaree = the support of the breath.
Hari is our kin, friend, companion and relative; He is the support of our life and the support of our breath.
The Lord is my Friend, my Very Best Friend, Companion and Relative. God is the Sustenance of the soul, the Support of the breath of life.
The Lord God is my friend, intimate, mate and kinsman, He is the sustenance of my soul and the mainstay of my vital-breath.
Kin, dearest friend, companion and every (bandhap) relative is the one Hari; He is the support of soul and breath and the giver of (dhaan) grain and the like.
U27W: Gahee = has grasped. Suaamee samrathah = of the all-powerful Master. ||9||
We have grasped the support of the all-powerful Master; Nanak, (His) servant, is for ever a sacrifice to Him. ||9||
I have grasped the Shelter and Support of my All-powerful Lord and Master; slave Nanak is forever a sacrifice to Him. ||9||
I have sought the protection of the Omnipotent Lord. Slave Nanak is ever a sacrifice to Him.
I have taken the shelter of such a powerful Master. Sri Guru ji says: we are for ever a sacrifice to that Hari. ||9||
QLJZ: Aavadh = with weapons. Charan kamal sang = with the lotus feet.
(The person who), joined to Hari's lotus feet, (has tasted) the taste of love cannot be cut down by weapons.
Weapons cannot cut that person who delights in the love of the Lord's Lotus Feet.
Whosoever enjoys the relish of the association of the love of the Lord's lotus feet he can be cut not with weapons.
The person who, through love for Prabhu's lotus feet, has gained the taste of that devotion is not cut down by the (aavadh) weapons of lust, anger and the rest, or of harsh words.
N2ZH: Daavan = with a rope (daaman = rope). Bandhio na jaat = cannot be bound. Bidhe = pierced. Daras mag = on the path of (Hari's) vision. Mag = on the path.
(The one whose) mind is pierced on the path of (Hari's) vision cannot be bound by a rope (to any other side).
Ropes cannot bind that person whose mind is pierced through by the Vision of the Lord's Way.
He, whose mind is pierced in the way of the Lord's vision, can be bound not with the rope.
The inner being of those who have (bidhe) joined the path of devotion for the sake of Parmeshvar's vision is not bound by the (daavan) rope of attachment.
6X6Z: Paavak = fire. Jario na jaat = cannot be burned. Jan dhoor = in the dust of the feet of the saints.
(The person who) stays attached to the dust of the saints' feet cannot be burned by fire;
Fire cannot burn that person who is attached to the dust of the feet of the Lord's humble servant.
Fire can burn not him, who is attached to the dust of the feet of the Lord's slave.
The person who stays attached to the (toorree) [sic: 'dhoorree', dust] of the feet of Vahiguru's servants is not burned by the fire of craving.
8KCJ: Neer = water. Bor = drown. Panth = path. Pag = feet.
(The one whose) feet walk on God's path cannot be drowned by water.
Water cannot drown that person whose feet walk on the Lord's Path.
The water can drown not the person, whose feet tread on the God's path.
Those who walk with their feet on Parmeshvar's path cannot be drowned by the water of things.
RTR7: Agh = sin. Chhide = are cut off. Khag = with the arrow. Dokh = vices. Panth = on the path. ||1||10||
O Nanak! (That person's) diseases, vices, sins and attachment — all these are cut off by the arrow of Hari's Name. ||1||10||
O Nanak, diseases, faults, sinful mistakes and emotional attachment are pierced by the Arrow of the Name. ||1||10||
Nanak, with the arrow of the Lord's Name, the ailments, blemishes, sins and worldly love are pierced through.
Sri Guru ji says: the body's diseases and faults, (agh) sins, attachment and other vices — all of these are (chhide) cut off by the sword of uttering Hari's Name. ||1||10||
6G5V: Bicharahi = reflect on. Anik = very many people. Saastr khatooaa = the six Shastras (Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta).
Countless people are making efforts of many kinds, reflecting on the six Shastras;
People are engaged in making all sorts of efforts; they contemplate the various aspects of the six Shaastras.
Men are engaged in making efforts in many ways. They greatly reflect upon the various aspects of the six Shashtras.
People are busy making efforts in many kinds of practices and means. Some, for much (khatooaa) earning — that is, gain — reflect again and again on the six Shastras.
XWNW: Bhramte = wander about. Sookham = weak. Deh = body. Bahu = many people. Bandhahi jatooaa = wear matted locks on the head.
Rubbing ash (on the body), many people wander to places of pilgrimage, and many have made their bodies weak (with austerities) and wear matted locks (on the head).
Rubbing ashes all over their bodies, they wander around at the various sacred shrines of pilgrimage; they fast until their bodies are emaciated, and braid their hair into tangled messes.
Besmearing their body with ashes, some wander at various pilgrim stations, some make their body thin lean and some blind their hair into many matted locks.
Some rub ash on the body and wander to many places of pilgrimage; some give up food and make the body thin; and some tie very great matted locks on the head.
8U30: Sagal = all (people). Prem = with love, with relish. Badhaai = spreads, stretches. Soot ke hatooaa = houses of thread, houses of threads, a web of threads.

Without taking Hari's Name, all these people suffer (all these displays become a net for them to be caught in), just as (the spider) with great relish spreads its web of threads (and is itself caught in it and killed by its own young).
Without devotional worship of the Lord, they all suffer in pain, caught in the tangled web of their love.
Without the Lord's meditation everyone suffers pain like the spider, which with love increases her web of yarn.

Just as a (hatooaa) shopkeeper, with growing fondness and with toil, makes laddoos of thread but does not eat them — that is, people read the Shastras with hardship but do not take in their conclusion. Or: just as the (hatooaa) spider draws out its own thread, weaves a web, is caught in it and dies, so the being binds itself by its own deeds. So the beings who do the practices above without Hari's worship always suffer the pains of birth and death through 'I' and 'mine'. So all pains are removed by Vahiguru's Name.
6PQT: Sompaaka = svayam paak, preparing one's food with one's own hands. Thaatahi = make. Bahu thatooaa = many forms, many contrivances, many garbs. ||2||11||20||

Many people do worship; they put the marks of the discus on the body, prepare their food with their own hands (for the sake of purity), and make many other contrivances of countless kinds (but without remembering the Name these too are in vain). ||2||11||20||
They perform worship ceremonies, draw ritual marks on their bodies, cook their own food fanatically, and make pompous shows of themselves in all sorts of ways. ||2||11||20||
Some perform worship, inscribe religious marks on their body, cook their own food and make ostentations in various ways.

Some go to Dwarka and other places and stamp the marks of the discus and such on the body, and some do worship. (Sompaaka) they keep the Chandrayan fast, or eat only after seeing the moon. Thus they set up many arrays of rituals; meaning, they make many kinds of contrivances. ||2||11||20|| ☬ Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji uttered these twenty Savaiye from his holy mouth: in nine of them he gives the praise of Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, and in eleven the teaching to the Bhatts. ☬ At that time, hearing the teaching from Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji, the Bhatts, who were the Vedas in form — all seventeen — gained knowledge, and, knowing that the time for the curse to end had come, having the vision of the True Gurus as Parmeshvar in person, uttered the praise of the True Gurus from Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji up to Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji. Now, first, they speak the praise of the First Patshahi, Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, as an invocation that unites him with Vishnu ji:
GBKY: Savaiye uttered in praise of Guru Nanak Sahib.
Swaiyas In Praise Of The First Mehl:
TCD7: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the True Guru's grace.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By the True Guru's grace, is He obtained.
VMDQ: Ik man = with one mind, one-pointedly. Dhiaai = remembering, meditating on. Bardaata = the giver of blessings.
Remembering with a one-pointed mind that Akal Purakh who is the giver of blessings,
Meditate single-mindedly on the Primal Lord God, the Bestower of blessings.
Contemplate on Lord with focused mind, who is the Bestower of blessings,
Making the mind one-pointed, I meditate on Parmeshvar, the Being who gives boons.
XR4A: Sant sahaar = the support of the saints. Bikhiaata = manifest, ever-present.
who is the support of the saints and who is ever-present,
He is the Helper and Support of the Saints, manifest forever.
and He is the Support of the saints and is ever manifest.
He, the (sahaar) support of the saints, is ever (bikhiaata) manifest.
BZ7V: Taas = His. Le = taking. Basaavau = I enshrine, may I enshrine.
I enshrine His feet in my heart,
Grasp His Feet and enshrine them in your heart.
Grasping His feet I enshrine them in my mind.
When I take the lotus feet of that Vahiguru and enshrine them in my heart — that is, meditate on those feet —
CBYC: Tau = then. Guroo Nanak gun = the virtues of Guru Nanak. ||1||
and (through their blessing) I sing the virtues of the supreme True Guru Nanak Dev ji. ||1||
Then, let us sing the Glorious Praises of the most exalted Guru Nanak. ||1||
Then sing I the praises of the most exalted Guru Nanak.
(tau) by that I sing the virtues of the True Guru Nanak Dev ji, (param) greatest of all. ||1||

2LMX: Rasik = lover. Naanak gur = O Guru Nanak! Tai = You. ||6||
